description: Generated by scripts/contracts/generate.mjs from schemas/. Do not edit.

schemas.title: Activity file
schemas.description: `activity.json` in the cache folder of the working copy: the last call through the local API or the MCP server that read or changed one element of the copy. Every API and MCP process of the copy rewrites it after such a call (the last writer wins). It is private (mode 0600, like `api.json`): scripts ask `workspace.activity`, which gives `access`. It holds no element content, only the UUID, repository, command, time and the hash of the element's file. Removing it is safe.

process.description: The writer: its process ID and 8 random hex digits, new whenever a workspace of the process starts recording. With `seq` it tells a new access from one already seen.

sha256.description: SHA-256 (hex) of the element's file as the call left it, so that a reader can tell whether it sees that content of the file yet.

access.description: One call that read or changed one element: which access made it, the command, its effect, when it ended and the element.

access.title: Access
access.description: The access the call came through. Only calls through the API and the MCP server are recorded.

command.title: Command
command.description: The catalog command of the call.

effect.title: Effect
effect.description: The effect of the command in the catalog.

element.title: Element
element.description: The element the call read or changed: its UUID and the repository of its file.

repository.title: Repository
repository.description: Workspace name of the repository of the element's file.

schemas.title: Agent connection file
schemas.description: `agent-<process>.json` in the cache folder of the working copy: one MCP server process of the copy whose client is connected or was connected last. The MCP server writes it when the client is connected: when it has written the successful answer to the client's `initialize`, or, for an MCP protocol revision without `initialize` (2026-07-28), when the first request naming that revision arrives, renews the file's modification time every second while it runs, and sets `ended` when it stops. A connection counts as connected while `ended` is null and the modification time is at most 3 s from now; a process that crashed stops counting 3 s after its last renewal. It is private (mode 0600, like `api.json`): scripts ask `workspace.agents`. Removing it is safe.

process.description: The MCP server process: its process ID and 8 random hex digits, new for every connection. The file name is `agent-<process>.json`; a file whose name does not match is ignored.

since.description: When the client connected: when the MCP server wrote the successful answer to its `initialize`, or, for an MCP protocol revision without `initialize` (2026-07-28), when the first request naming that revision arrived.

ended.description: When the connection ended cleanly (the client closed standard input, the server was stopped); null while it runs, and after a crash.

client.description: The name the client gave when it connected (`clientInfo.name`), as text: each run of white space one space, control, format and surrogate characters other than the joiners removed, trimmed, cut at a character boundary to at most 40 characters (grapheme clusters, so an accented letter or a composed emoji counts as one and is not split) and at most 400 UTF-16 code units. null when it gave none or nothing is left. A longer name in the file is cut when it is read.

schemas.title: API endpoint file
schemas.description: `api.json` in the cache folder of the working copy (`<OS cache>/reqseq/<sha256 of the absolute workspace root>/`): where the running local API of `reqseq serve api` listens, and its token. Written at start with mode 0600; a client reads it and sends `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. The API listens on loopback only. A file left behind by a stopped API names a port nobody listens on.

port.description: The port the API listens on.

token.description: 256 random bits, base64url without padding; new at every start.

urls.description: Base URLs, one per loopback address the API listens on (`::1` only where the machine has IPv6).

pid.description: Process ID of the API. While it runs, a second API for the same working copy asks the URLs before it starts; when it does not run, the file is stale and is replaced.

schemas.title: Baseline file
schemas.description: A baseline is a YAML file with name, date, the stored selection, the commit of every repository involved and ID plus version of every element in the selection. ReqSeq writes the file once and never changes or replaces it; a person commits it with Git. No reason or approval field. The metamodel of the baseline is given by the commit of the metamodel repository. ReqSeq writes the keys in this order, one entry per line; a file in another layout is read too, more slowly.

date.description: When the baseline was created, in UTC without fractions. Its day is the UTC day.

repositories.description: The repositories of the selected elements, the main repository and the metamodel's, each once with its HEAD commit.

name.description: Workspace name of the repository.

repository.description: The repository of the copy, relative to the repository of the baseline file: given when they differ or the UUID has copies in several repositories.

elements.description: Sorted by id, then repository (code units; none first), each element copy once; one flow mapping per line.

name.description: Name of a baseline, unique in the workspace ignoring case and Unicode normal form. The file name is the name made portable, as attachment names; a taken file name gets -2, -3, ….

storedSelection.description: The selection the baseline was created with, which is read again when the baseline, its evidence and validation status or the changes of a variant since it are shown or compared. ReqSeq writes it canonical: `where` as filter.save writes it, a saved filter as its `where` and `view`, `package` and `view` as `{ id, title }` in the repository of the file and `{ id, repository }` elsewhere, the title at baseline time; `ids` items without title.

ids.description: A UUID in the repository of the file, `{ id, repository }` elsewhere; one per line, read line by line like `elements`.

filter.description: Name of a saved filter, as an older or hand-written file may hold; read with the filter as it is now. Not written.

view.description: `core` (a reference like any other, so not a separate constituent), or the variant as `{ id, title }` or a hand-written reference.

storedRef.description: An element of the stored selection: as written, or any reference a person may write by hand.

title.description: Title of the element at baseline time, for people; not read, the element is found by `id`.

elsewhere.description: An element in another repository than the file's.

repository.description: Workspace name of the repository of the element.

schemas.title: Shared definitions
schemas.description: Building blocks used by all ReqSeq file formats and commands. See docs/adr/0004 and 0005.

criterionKey.description: A criterion key: a lower-case letter a to z, then 3 to 15 lower-case letters a to z or digits.

criterionRef.description: An acceptance criterion as a record names it: its criterion key, or its number, the position in the version the record names, counted from 1.

textMarks.description: Matched words in a text, to highlight: UTF-16 code-unit offsets into the text, `end` exclusive, sorted and not overlapping.

uuid.description: Element ID: random UUID version 4, lower case, never changes.

shortId.description: Display ID: type prefix, dash, the trailing hex characters of the UUID with dashes removed, at least 6, more until unique in the workspace. The file name uses 12.

elementRef.description: UUID, short ID or identifier (e.g. SR-036), any case; several matches give ref.ambiguous.

uuidRef.description: A UUID version 4 as a caller gives it, in any case; ReqSeq stores it in lower case.

elementId.description: A reference to an element as ReqSeq writes it in outputs: UUID or short ID in their canonical form.

countedElement.description: An element that a number of a write command's output counts.

repository.title: Repository
repository.description: Workspace name of the repository of its file.

keptDefinition.description: A property or status definition that no type has any more and that stays, as elements of any type, also of a type the metamodel does not know, hold it.

kind.title: Kind
kind.description: property, or status.

count.title: Elements holding it
count.description: The elements that have the status, or whose file holds the property key, also with an empty value; those of `elements`.

elements.title: Elements holding it
elements.description: The elements `count` counts, in store order.

elementName.description: How an output names an element it gives elsewhere by UUID only, for people: its short ID, its identifier when it has one and its title, as element.list gives them.

repository.title: Repository
repository.description: Workspace name of the repository of its file.

identifier.title: Identifier
identifier.description: Its identifier, when it has one.

version.description: The version: its normal form (`n1`, `n2`, …), a colon, first 16 hex characters of the SHA-256 over the canonical content. Example: n1:9f86d081884c7d65.

fileSha256.description: SHA-256 of the bytes of an element file, lower-case hex: a write precondition, never stored and not a version.

key.description: Fixed metamodel key of a type, property, relation kind or status value. Readable English, lower case, dashes.

keyOrName.description: A metamodel value as a person gives it: its key or its display name, in any case (`Obsolete` names the status obsolete). ReqSeq stores the key.

relationTarget.description: Target of a relation as stored in the source file. Within the same repository: `id`, `version`, `title`. Across repositories: `id`, `version`, `repository` (workspace name of the target's repository), never title or text. Written as one flow mapping per line.

title.description: Title of the target as stored; only within the same repository.

repository.description: Workspace name of the target's repository; required across repositories, absent within one.

relationRefs.description: Relations a caller gives to element.create or element.update by relation kind key, each with the element reference of its target or a list of them (UUID, short ID or identifier, as relation.add takes them). ReqSeq checks them as relation.add does and stores each target with its current version.

relationTargetInput.description: Target of a relation as a caller gives it to element.create, element.update or element.bulkUpdate. Only `id` and, across repositories, `repository` name the target; `id` is an element reference like the one relation.add takes (UUID, short ID or identifier), and ReqSeq writes the target's UUID. A plain string item is the same as `{ id }` with it. A target the property already stores keeps its stored version and form; for every other target ReqSeq writes its current version and the title (same repository) or repository (across repositories) itself. A given `version` or `title` is ignored.

repository.description: Workspace name of the target's repository; absent for the source's own repository. A short ID or identifier is resolved in it.

item.description: The item under test: the concrete build or sample that was checked. No white space at either end and no control characters other than tab, line feed and carriage return.

dateTime.description: A date and time with time zone (RFC 3339 date-time), for example 2026-10-26T09:30:00Z.

commit.description: Full Git object ID (SHA-1 or SHA-256).

relativePath.description: Path relative to the repository or file it appears in, forward slashes, no `..` segments.

localPath.description: A file or folder on the local machine, relative or absolute. CLI: relative to the current folder (the CLI makes it absolute before the call); API and MCP: relative to the workspace root, and only inside the repositories of the workspace, also after symbolic links are followed; `~` is not expanded. App: like API and MCP relative to the workspace root, any path, and `~` at the start stands for the home folder.

problem.description: A problem, also a hint (a problem of severity warning about one element). Commands return problems as data so every access shows the same result.

file.title: File
file.description: The file the problem is about; relative to `repository` when that is given.

repository.title: Repository
repository.description: Workspace name of the repository the problem is about (element files of several repositories, the metamodel repository, a repository Git cannot read); `file`, when given, is relative to that repository.

elementRepository.title: Repository of the element
elementRepository.description: Workspace name of the repository of the element the problem is about, when `repository` and `file` name another file (the evidence record of `evidence.outdated`). With `elementFile` it names one copy of a UUID several files share.

elementFile.title: File of the element
elementFile.description: The file of the element the problem is about, relative to `elementRepository`; given with it.

elementShortId.title: Short ID of the element
elementShortId.description: Short ID of the element `elementId` names, for display; given on every problem that names an element of the workspace, by every command that has read the elements.

elementIdentifier.title: Identifier of the element
elementIdentifier.description: Identifier of the element `elementId` names (the value of its property with the meaning `identifier`), for display next to `elementShortId`; given with it when the element has one.

elementTitle.title: Title of the element
elementTitle.description: Title of the element `elementId` names, for display next to `elementShortId`; given by hint.list on the hints of its page, for the element `elementShortId` names; empty when the element has no title that is a text, or the metamodel gives no property the meaning `title`.

targetRepository.title: Repository of the target
targetRepository.description: Workspace name of the repository the target `targetId` names was resolved in; given when the problem's target is one element there.

targetShortId.title: Short ID of the target
targetShortId.description: Short ID of the element `targetId` names, for display; given with `targetRepository` when that UUID names one element there, by every command that has read the elements. A missing, ambiguous or unresolved target gets none.

targetIdentifier.title: Identifier of the target
targetIdentifier.description: Identifier of the element `targetId` names (the value of its property with the meaning `identifier`), for display next to `targetShortId`; given with it when the element has one.

targetTitle.title: Title of the target
targetTitle.description: Title of the element `targetId` names, for display next to `targetShortId`; given by hint.list where `targetRepository` names one element with that UUID, empty as `elementTitle`.

storedDate.title: Date of the stored version
storedDate.description: Date of the stored version; null when unknown.

currentDate.title: Date of the current version
currentDate.description: Date of the current version; null when unknown.

storedCommit.title: Commit of the stored version
storedCommit.description: Object name of the commit that started the stored version, given with `storedDate` and null exactly when it is: with `currentCommit`, `git diff <storedCommit> <currentCommit> -- <file>` shows what changed. A pointer valid at the current HEAD, never stored.

currentCommit.title: Commit of the current version
currentCommit.description: Object name of the commit that started the current version, given with `currentDate` and null exactly when it is (as `storedCommit`).

hintId.title: Hint ID
hintId.description: Stable ID of a confirmable hint; on the hint.* problems of hint.confirm, the ID as given.

key.title: Key
key.description: The key (property or relation kind) a problem about one key is about, so that an access can tell it without reading the message: the relation kind or property of a count hint (`relation.too-many`, `relation.too-few`; `element.too-many-items`), the acceptance criteria of `element.criterion-key-missing`, `element.criterion-key-duplicate` and `element.criterion-key-invalid`, the property of `element.text-emptied`, `element.wrong-value-kind`, `element.missing-required`, `element.duplicate-identifier` and `element.statement-without-text`, the property of `element.unknown-property` when its key has the form of a metamodel key (a frontmatter key can be any text), the key of the relation item of `relation.outdated`, `variant.core-changed`, `relation.missing-target`, `relation.cross-repository-title`, `relation.not-allowed`, `relation.target-superseded`, `variant.superseded-in-validity` and `variant.nested`, and the property marked `markdown` that holds a reference of `relation.outdated`, `relation.missing-target`, `relation.unresolved-link` or `relation.reference-style`. A reference in the text has none.

place.title: Place
place.description: Where a confirmable hint (`relation.outdated`, `variant.core-changed`) is, as data next to its `hintId`: with `key`, `targetId` and `storedVersion` it names what the ID names.

in.title: In
in.description: `relation`: an item of the relation kind or relation-valued property `key`. `text`: an inline reference in the text, or with `key` in a value of that property marked `markdown`.

repository.title: Repository
repository.description: The repository the item or reference names, as it writes it; absent when it names none.

occurrence.title: Occurrence
occurrence.description: `text` only: the reference is the n-th (from 1) of that text with the same target, repository and stored version (`&n=` of the hint ID).

targetType.title: Target type
targetType.description: The target type of the limit a count hint is about.

count.title: Count
count.description: How many relations the element has that the limit counts, how many entries its list property has, or how many of its acceptance criteria have no criterion key (`element.criterion-key-missing`).

criteria.title: Acceptance criteria
criteria.description: The acceptance criteria of the element the problem is about, with number, criterion key and text, each left out where it does not apply, as the message names them: the criteria whose status is outdated (`evidence.outdated`), the two that carry one key and the one with a key of another form (`element.criterion-key-duplicate`, `element.criterion-key-invalid`), and those a record names that the version it names lacks (`evidence.unknown-criterion`, key or number as named, without text).

limit.title: Limit
limit.description: The maximum (`relation.too-many`, `element.too-many-items`) or minimum (`relation.too-few`) the metamodel sets.

view.title: View
view.description: The view whose verification or validation status an `evidence.outdated` hint is about: `core` or the UUID of the variant, also when the record it names holds in every variant.

problemCode.description: Stable codes. New codes are added here first, in the PR that needs them.

error.description: Error of a command call. Same codes over CLI (stderr, exit code), API (HTTP body) and MCP (tool error). `command.not-implemented`: the command is in the catalog, but this ReqSeq version does not implement it yet (a later stage).

details.description: Facts about the error that a client can read without parsing `message`; they depend on the code. For `workspace.not-found`: `file`, the missing workspace file; `below`, the folders one level below that hold one; else `next`, the next step (`#/$defs/nextStep`) that creates a workspace in the folder, when `workspace.init` can create it there. For `tool.guide` with `write` when a place of the skill file was not written, whatever the code: `command` and `places`, each place in order as the output lists it, a place not written with `error` (`code`, `message`, `details`) instead of `action`. For `internal` they may be `command`, the command called; `aborted: true` when its caller aborted the call; `errors` when the output of the command does not match its schema; and `cause` when an unexpected error caused it (one that is not reported as an error of ReqSeq), with its `name`, its `code` when it has one, and the first line of its `message`, at most 160 characters, absolute paths shown as `<workspace>/…` or `<path>`.

answer.title: Answer
answer.description: One English sentence on what the command found, counted or did, such as `Checked 4 elements and found 1 warning.`. ReqSeq builds it from the output and the input, so it is the same through every access, and it names no time relative to reading it. The command line prints it as the first line of its text output, except for an output that is a format such as Mermaid.

incomplete.description: True when a result is incomplete because targets are in repositories that are not available locally.
incomplete.title: Incomplete

selection.description: Which elements a command works on: a saved filter, an inline filter, a package, a baseline, the output of a read command or explicit IDs, also named with their repository, optionally seen through a variant view.

inRepository.title: IDs with their repository
inRepository.description: Explicit IDs named with their repository: each a UUID and the workspace name of the repository of its file, for every element with that UUID there. An item that names none is ref.unknown.

repository.title: Repository
repository.description: Workspace name of the repository.

baseline.title: Baseline
baseline.description: Name of a baseline, or its file name in the baselines folder (with or without .yaml).

outputSelection.description: The elements of the output field of a read command marked `x-elements: "answer"`, over all pages; with `count`, the elements one number of its output counts.

count.title: Number
count.description: A number of the output that counts elements (its `outputFields` entry has `elements`, neither `true` nor `answer`): the elements it counts for this input, over all pages. Without it, the answer's.

field.title: Field
field.description: Its path in `outputFields`, `[]` per list, no position: `degree.counts.open`, `groups[].count`.

key.title: Entries
key.description: Per `[]` of `field`, outermost first: the entry by the fields its `keys` names, one it lacks left out. An entry the output lacks gives no elements.

searchFieldKey.description: A field a search is restricted to: `title`, `text`, `properties`, `id` or the key of a property; element.search checks the key against the metamodel, and element.searchFields lists the keys it takes.

groupKey.description: A key to group a list by: `type`, `status`, `package` or a property key.

listGroup.description: One group of a grouped list and where its rows are.

value.title: Value
value.description: Left out for the last group, the elements without a value. The type key, the status, the short ID of the package or target, the choice key, else the value as written. With a filter on it (`type` with subtypes false, `status`, `package`, a property condition with op eq) it selects the group's elements, except those that write a choice by its display name.

name.title: Name
name.description: Display name of a type, status or choice of the metamodel.

title.title: Title
title.description: Title of a package or target, when it has one.

identifier.title: Identifier
identifier.description: Identifier of a package or target, when it has one.

unavailable.title: Unavailable targets
unavailable.description: Only in the last group of a grouping by package or another relation property: its elements that name targets, none of them available (not on this machine or not in the workspace).

count.title: Rows
count.description: Rows in the group: its elements or hits.

offset.title: Offset
offset.description: Row of its first element in the grouped list: the group holds the rows offset to offset + count - 1.

viewId.description: A view as ReqSeq writes it in outputs: `core` or the canonical UUID or short ID of a variant.

view.description: `core`, a variant ID, or absent for all. A variant's view: the core requirements it neither excludes nor replaces, plus those that apply in it; elements without validity property are in every view.

verificationStatus.description: The verification status. `indirect` = indirectly verified via children.

validationStatus.description: The validation status. `inconclusive` = the validation could not decide.

reqifObject.description: An object of a ReqIF file by its IDENTIFIER in the source, with the UUID of its element when there is one.

identifier.title: Identifier
identifier.description: The IDENTIFIER of the object in the ReqIF file.

reqifLoss.description: Content of a ReqIF file that is not taken over without loss: the object, its element when there is one, a stable code and the reason.

identifier.title: Identifier
identifier.description: IDENTIFIER of the SPEC-OBJECT, SPEC-RELATION or SPECIFICATION.

kind.title: Object kind
kind.description: Which kind of object is affected.

reqifUnmapped.description: A type, attribute, relation type or enumeration value of a ReqIF file that the mapping neither maps nor omits. `source` is its LONG-NAME or IDENTIFIER; `sourceType` the SPEC-OBJECT-TYPE of an attribute or value, `attribute` the attribute of a value.

kind.title: What is not mapped
kind.description: What is not mapped: a type, an attribute, a relation type or an enumeration value.

source.title: Name in the source
source.description: Its LONG-NAME or IDENTIFIER in the source.

sourceType.title: Source type
sourceType.description: The SPEC-OBJECT-TYPE of an attribute or value.

outputPath.title: Path
outputPath.description: A file or folder as an output names it: relative to the workspace root or to the repository the field names, with `/`, or absolute where the field says so.

fieldDifference.title: Difference
fieldDifference.description: What changed in an element between two of its files, by the rule of the HTML export: the text, each acceptance criterion matched by its criterion key, and each property that counts to the version under the metamodel of the local copy, each with its old and new wording in full, and the relations added and removed. The stored version and title of a target never count. Empty lists where nothing changed.

text.title: Text
text.description: The old and the new text; left out when the text did not change.

before.title: Before
before.description: The text at the commit of the baseline.

after.title: After
after.description: The text in the local copy.

criteria.title: Acceptance criteria
criteria.description: Each acceptance criterion that changed, was added (no `before`) or was removed (no `after`); a criterion without text has the wording "".

key.title: Criterion key
key.description: Its criterion key, where one of the two files gives it one.

numberBefore.title: Number before
numberBefore.description: Its number in the old file, counted from 1.

numberAfter.title: Number after
numberAfter.description: Its number in the new file, counted from 1.

before.title: Before
before.description: Its wording in the old file; left out when it was added.

after.title: After
after.description: Its wording in the new file; left out when it was removed.

properties.title: Properties
properties.description: Each property that changed, by its key; a list one item per line after `- `, any value other than a string as JSON, and no `before` or `after` where it is absent.

key.title: Property
key.description: The key of the property.

before.title: Before
before.description: Its value in the old file; left out where it is absent.

after.title: After
after.description: Its value in the new file; left out where it is absent.

changedRelation.title: Relation
changedRelation.description: A relation target that was added or removed, as the file stores it.

kind.title: Relation
kind.description: The relation kind or relation property key.

id.title: Target
id.description: The ID of the target as the file stores it: a UUID, unless a file at the commit of the baseline holds another value.

repository.title: Repository
repository.description: Workspace name of the target's repository, where the entry stores one.

title.title: Title
title.description: The title the entry stores, where it stores one.

baselineSince.title: Changes since the baseline
baselineSince.description: A baseline and its elements per state since it, as baseline.get gives them for it: the same numbers over all pages.

name.title: Baseline
name.description: Name of the baseline.

file.title: File
file.description: Relative to the workspace root, / as separator.

repository.title: Repository
repository.description: The repository that holds the file.

view.title: View
view.description: The view of the stored selection; left out for the core.

selectionKnown.title: Selection stored
selectionKnown.description: The file stores a selection. Without it no element is added or removed, and `counts` has no `added` and `removed`.

counts.title: Elements per state
counts.description: Elements per state over all pages, as `counts` of baseline.get.

removed.title: Removed
removed.description: Elements that left the selection since the baseline; left out without a stored selection.

added.title: Added
added.description: Elements that joined the selection since the baseline; left out without a stored selection.

missing.title: Missing
missing.description: Elements of the baseline that are not found.

inaccessible.title: Not on this machine
inaccessible.description: Elements of the baseline in a repository that is not on this machine.

problems.title: Problems
problems.description: In baseline.prepare: the problems baseline.get gives for the baseline, apart from those of the check.

nextStep.title: Next step
nextStep.description: A command to run next: the command, the input fields known already and those still to give. Every access shows the same step in its own form: the command line as a call with the open fields in angle brackets.

command.title: Command
command.description: Name of the command in the catalog.

input.title: Known input
input.description: The input fields known already, with their values; a path is absolute.

open.title: Open fields
open.description: The input fields still to give, in the order of the command's arguments.

workspace.title: Workspace
workspace.description: Absolute path of the workspace the step runs in, when the step names one (the new workspace after `workspace.init`).

schemas.title: Data of a state as JSON
schemas.description: Output of `data.export` for external evaluation tools such as Grafana or DuckDB. The JSON Lines form (`data export --jsonl`, the API with `Accept: application/x-ndjson`, and the file `<commit>.jsonl` or `<commit>-dirty.jsonl` that `data.store` writes) has one `#/$defs/line` per element instead: the state fields `reqseq-data`, `commit`, `dirty`, `repositories` and `incomplete`, then the element. Also defines the element and relation shapes all commands return.

answer.description: The answer of `data.export`, which its output always has; not in the file that `data.store` writes nor in the JSON Lines form.

reqseq-data.title: Format version
reqseq-data.description: The version of this format. 2: with `commit` and `dirty` at the top level and the JSON Lines form (`$defs/line`). 3: a successor's relation has the meaning `succession` instead of `replacement`. 4: every line of the JSON Lines form also carries `repositories` and `incomplete`. 5: a record names a criterion by key or number, and `notVerified` names each criterion with number, key and text.

commit.title: Commit
commit.description: The commit of the state: HEAD of the main repository (the one with the workspace file), after which data.store names its file; left out when Git cannot tell.

dirty.title: Uncommitted changes
dirty.description: `false` only when every available repository has a known commit and is known clean (see `repositories[].dirty`), the rule by which data.store adds `-dirty` to the name of its file.

generated.title: Exported at
generated.description: Time of the export, UTC, in seconds.

selection.title: Selection
selection.description: The selection as given; left out when none was given (every element).

repositories.title: Repositories
repositories.description: The repositories of the workspace file, in its order.

incomplete.description: The data may lack elements or records: a repository of the workspace is not on this machine (its entry in `repositories` has `available: false`), so its elements and the records of its evidence locations are missing, or a condition of the selection met a target in a repository the workspace file does not list. A baselines folder that is not on this machine holds no baseline: `selection.baseline` then gives `input.invalid`.

elements.title: Elements
elements.description: Every element of the selection in workspace order, superseded ones included, without text; in data.export each with `validity`, `packages`, `verification` and its relations with `currentVersion` and `outdated`.

repository.description: One repository of the workspace file with its state, in `repositories` of the JSON form and of every line.

name.title: Repository
name.description: Workspace name of the repository.

available.title: Available
available.description: The repository is on this machine.

commit.title: Commit
commit.description: HEAD of the repository, as `workspace.status` gives it; left out when Git cannot tell.

dirty.title: Uncommitted changes
dirty.description: Uncommitted changes, by content against `commit`, to the files the data is made of (workspace file, YAML files of the metamodel, filter and baseline folders, element files and the files they embed, also ones Git ignores; not evidence records); left out when Git cannot tell.

element.description: An element as the commands give it: the fields of `$defs/elementFields`, and no others.

elementPart.description: Some fields of an element (element.list `fields`): `id`, `shortId` and `repository` always, the others of `$defs/elementFields` when asked for and given, and no others.

line.description: One line of the JSON Lines form of data.export (`data export --jsonl`, the API with `Accept: application/x-ndjson`) and of the file of data.store: `reqseq-data`, `commit`, `dirty`, `repositories` and `incomplete` of the state first, as at the top level of the JSON form, then the fields of one element, unchanged.

repositories.description: As `repositories` of the JSON form: the commit of each available repository, and which repository is not on this machine.

elementFields.description: The fields of an element, shared by `$defs/element`, `$defs/line` and `$defs/elementPart`, which say which are required; open, so never used alone.

identifier.title: Identifier
identifier.description: The value of its property with the meaning `identifier` (an ID from another source such as SR-036), for display next to `shortId`; left out when it has none. The property itself stays under `properties`.

status.title: Status
status.description: The status key as written; left out when the element has none (a type without status).

title.title: Title
title.description: Title of the element; empty without one.

text.title: Text
text.description: Markdown text below the frontmatter, without the blank line after the closing `---`. Left out by list commands unless asked for.

version.title: Version
version.description: The current version of the element. Left out when it cannot be computed (its file no longer holds the element, an embedded image cannot be read, a counted value has no normal form); then `problems` says why (file.faulty).

versionDate.title: Version date
versionDate.description: Date of the version from Git (shown instead of the hash): the committer date of the newest commit that started this version (no parent of it had the version), in UTC as YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ. null when no commit has it (uncommitted content), when Git cannot tell (no git, not a repository, no commit, shallow clone) and when Git did not answer in time. Left out when `version` is left out.

repository.title: Repository
repository.description: Workspace name of the repository of its file.

file.title: File
file.description: Path relative to the repository.

readOnly.title: Read-only
readOnly.description: Unknown type, invalid metamodel or read-only repository.

validity.title: Validity
validity.description: Given by data.export: the UUIDs of the variants the property with the meaning `validity` names, in its order; `[]` = the core and every variant. Left out when the metamodel has no validity property.

packages.title: Packages
packages.description: Given by data.export: the UUIDs of the packages the property with the meaning `packages` names, in its order; `[]` when none. Left out when the metamodel has no packages property.

replacedBy.title: Replaced by
replacedBy.description: Given only for a core requirement: each variant that replaces it and the replacing requirement, one entry per pair; a variant that also excludes it is only in excludedBy. Left out when empty.

excludedBy.title: Excluded by
excludedBy.description: The variants that exclude this core requirement. Left out when empty.

emergent.title: Emergent
emergent.description: True when the element's property with the meaning `emergent` holds the choice `yes`; only true is given, left out otherwise. An emergent requirement is never `indirect`: without an own verification record in a view it is `open` there.

properties.title: Properties
properties.description: All other properties by key, unknown ones included.

relations.title: Relations
relations.description: The element's own relations, then the targets of its properties of kind `relation` (`property: true`), then the incoming relations (`direction: in`); in stage 1 only the relations with the meaning `succession` from the successors of an element with a status marked invalid. The targets of `validity` and `packages` also appear in `validity` and `packages` in data.export. `currentVersion` and `outdated` are given by data.export and trace.matrix.

verification.title: Verification status
verification.description: Verification status, one entry per view the requirement is in by the view rule: the core when it has no validity, each variant it is in; none for a variant that excludes or replaces it or whose status the metamodel marks invalid.

validation.title: Validation status
validation.description: The Validierungsstatus from the validation records of the core (no `variant`) against the element's current version; the newest record of that version decides, only records of older versions give `outdated`. Given for every element whose type has the meaning `need` (`open` without record) and for every element whose type has the meaning `requirement` with a validation record; left out otherwise, also for a validation record of any other element, which counts for no status. Never inherited from children; never the element's `status`. `inconclusive` when that record is inconclusive; on a tie at the newest date `failed` before `inconclusive` before `validated`.

validationReason.title: Reason of the validation status
validationReason.description: The `reason` of the inconclusive record that decides `validation`; given exactly when `validation` is `inconclusive`.

kind.title: Relation kind
kind.description: Key of the relation kind, or of the property of kind `relation` (e.g. `validity`, `packages`) that stores the target; such a property's targets also stay under `properties` as stored, and their entries have `property: true` and no `meaning`.

property.title: Property
property.description: `kind` is the key of a property of kind `relation`, not of a relation kind. Left out for relation kinds.

direction.title: Direction
direction.description: `out`: the element stores the relation. `in`: another element stores it and points at this one.

repository.title: Repository of the other end
repository.description: Workspace name of the repository of the other end: the one the relation names, the source's own when it names none; for `direction: in` the source's (the other end: a successor, or the source of any incoming relation). Given in every `targetState`, as the name it stores for `inaccessible` and `unknown-repository`; left out only when the stored `repository` is not text. With `id` it names the target (`element.get` with `ref` and `repository`; an `ambiguous` target also needs `file`; for `unknown-repository` the name is not a repository of the workspace).

shortId.title: Short ID of the other end
shortId.description: Of the other end when it is available; of a target in a repository that is not on this machine with the prefix `UNKNOWN`, since its type is not known.

identifier.title: Identifier of the other end
identifier.description: Identifier of the other end, only when it is available locally and has one.

title.title: Title of the other end
title.description: Only when the other end is available locally, also across repositories, where the file stores no title.

targetState.title: Target state
targetState.description: Where the other end is: `available` = exactly one element with the UUID in the repository the relation names (the source's own when it names none); `inaccessible` = that repository is in the workspace file but not on this machine; `missing` = the repository is here, the UUID is not in it; `ambiguous` = several files there share the UUID; `unknown-repository` = the workspace file lists no repository of that name, or `repository` is not text.

outdated.title: Outdated
outdated.description: The stored version of the other end differs from its current version.

evidenceRecord.description: An evidence record as commands return it: the fields of `evidence-record.schema.json` with the same rules, from a Markdown record or a JUnit test case alike, without the format marker `reqseq-record`; `test-case` is `testCase`.

element.title: Element
element.description: Verification: a requirement. Validation: a need or a requirement.

kind.title: Record kind
kind.description: Verification or validation.

variant.title: Variant
variant.description: Variant the record holds for. Absent: the core, and also every variant the element applies in when the element's repository is marked `variant-independent`.

item.title: Item under test
item.description: The item under test. Required for verification, optional for validation.

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: The reason for an `inconclusive` validation record; given exactly with that result.

evidence.title: Evidence document
evidence.description: Where the evidence document is: relative path, file URL or any URI.

testCase.title: Test case
testCase.description: Optional test case name or ID: the `test-case` of a Markdown record, the `name` of a JUnit test case.

source.title: Record format
source.description: The format of the record file: a Markdown record (`evidence-record.schema.json`) or a test case of a JUnit XML file.

repository.title: Repository
repository.description: Workspace name of the repository of the record file (an evidence location of the workspace file).

file.title: Record file
file.description: The record file, relative to its repository, `/` as separator.

line.title: Line
line.description: The line of the `<testcase>` in a JUnit file; 1 for a Markdown record.

evidenceSource.title: Evidence document
evidenceSource.description: Where the evidence document of the record is, as a person reads it: `evidence` when given and not empty; else the record file, `<repository>/<file>` (`<file>` alone without `repository`) and `:<line>` when `line` is given; left out when the record has neither. Not an evidence location of the workspace file. Text only, never opened.

className.title: Class name
className.description: The `classname` of a JUnit test case; with `testCase` it names the test case. Left out for a Markdown record.

criteria.title: Acceptance criteria
criteria.description: The acceptance criteria the record holds for, by criterion key or by number (the position in the record's `version`, counted from 1), each once: numbers ascending, then keys in code-unit order: `criteria` of a Markdown record, the `reqseq:criterion` properties of a JUnit test case for this element. Left out: every criterion. Never on a validation record.

criterionNames.title: Acceptance criteria
criterionNames.description: Each item of `criteria`, in its order, named with number, key and text: the number is the position in the current version, whose criteria are counted; a key the current version lacks has no number and the text of the record's version; a number of a record's version in which that criterion has no key keeps that number and, where Git has that version, that version's text, without key. Filled by the commands that list records: `evidence.list` (also in its test cases), `trace.chain`, `trace.matrix`, `trace.affected` and `evidence.record`, each counting the current version, and `baseline.get` in `later`, counting the baseline's version; not in the data export, which has no records.

baselines.title: Baselines
baselines.description: The `name` of every baseline file (`baseline.schema.json`, in the `baselines` folder of the workspace file) that lists the element of the record with its version, in file order, each name once. Only `evidence.list` fills it.

testCase.description: A test case seen from one element: the test case named by JUnit `classname` and `name`, or by the `test-case` of Markdown records, with the records of that one element. Every `<testcase>` of a JUnit file and every Markdown record is one execution: a file that holds the test case twice (a rerun) gives two. A test case that names several elements is listed at each of them, each time with that element's records only, since the version and so whether a record is outdated belong to the element. A test case whose only appearances are skipped JUnit test cases (`<skipped>` gives no record) has `executed: false` and no executions.

name.title: Test case
name.description: The JUnit `name`, or the `test-case` of the Markdown records.

className.title: Class name
className.description: The JUnit `classname`; left out for a test case of Markdown records.

elements.title: Named elements
elements.description: Every element the test case names, in any of its executions and skipped appearances, each once.

executed.title: Executed
executed.description: The test case has at least one record of this element.

executions.title: Executions
executions.description: The records of this element from this test case, newest first (by `date`, then repository, file and line); empty when `executed` is false.

last.title: Last execution
last.description: The newest execution, `executions[0]`, the first in index order of several equally new ones; left out when `executed` is false.

rowVerification.description: What a row of a list shows of its element's verification, the fields a node of trace.graph carries for it, in the view of the list's selection (the selection's, else its saved filter's, else the core), the view evidence.degree counts the same selection in: its element, and nothing else for an element with none of them.

repository.title: Repository
repository.description: Workspace name of the repository of its file.

file.title: File
file.description: Path relative to the repository.

verification.title: Verification status
verification.description: The verification status of a requirement in that view, one entry; left out for any other element and for a requirement without a status there.

criteria.title: Criteria
criteria.description: The count of a requirement's progress ring, as trace.graph gives it (`criteria` of a node).

degree.title: Verification degree
degree.description: For a need, the verification degree of the requirements derived directly from it, as trace.graph gives it (`degree` of a node).

verificationEntry.description: The verification status of a requirement in one view: `element` `verification` gives one per view it lists (none for a variant whose status the metamodel marks invalid), `trace.matrix` one for its view.

missingChildren.title: Children without verification
missingChildren.description: For a requirement without own verification record in the view whose status is `open`: its counted children (derivation children whose type has the meaning `requirement`, whose status is not marked invalid and that apply in the view) that are `open`, `failed` or `outdated`; direct children only, in child order, each UUID once (twins in several repositories, share one); left out when there is none.

criteria.title: Criteria
criteria.description: How many of the requirement's acceptance criteria its own records in the view verify, for example 2 of 3. Only for a requirement whose status comes from its own records and whose current version has acceptance criteria (the property with the meaning `acceptance-criteria`); left out for a status from the children and without criteria.

criterionName.description: An acceptance criterion as an output names it: number, criterion key and text, each left out where it does not apply.

criterion.title: Number
criterion.description: The number: the position in the version whose criteria are counted, counted from 1.

text.title: Text
text.description: The text of the acceptance criterion.

criterionEntry.description: An acceptance criterion of the current version of a requirement: its number, criterion key, text and the reference a test name uses.

criterion.title: Number
criterion.description: The number: the position in the current version, counted from 1, so the numbers have no gaps.

key.title: Criterion key
key.description: The criterion key; left out when the criterion has none.

text.title: Text
text.description: The text of the acceptance criterion.

reference.title: Test name reference
reference.description: The reference for a test name, `[<name>/AK-<key>]`: the name is the identifier of the requirement when a test name with it leads back to this requirement (no `/`, `[` or `]`, not blank, no other element has it), else its short ID. Left out for a criterion without key and for both criteria that carry the same key.

criterionReferences.description: The acceptance criteria of a requirement's current version with their references for test names, in their order. Given for an element whose type has the meaning `requirement` and that has acceptance criteria, each a text; left out otherwise.

property.title: Property
property.description: The key of the property with the meaning `acceptance-criteria` that holds them.

criteriaCount.description: How many acceptance criteria of a requirement are verified: a criterion is verified when the newest record for it of the current version passed (a record that names no criterion counts for every one).

verified.title: Verified criteria
verified.description: The number of verified acceptance criteria.

notVerified.title: Criteria not verified
notVerified.description: The criteria that are not verified (open, failed or outdated), by number ascending, each with its key and text; left out when every criterion is verified.

verificationDegree.description: The verification degree of a selection in one view. Counted are the requirements of the selection (type with the meaning `requirement`) whose status the metamodel does not mark invalid and that have a verification status in the view.

share.title: Share
share.description: (verified + indirect) / total, unrounded; left out when total is 0. Shown as a percentage rounded down to one decimal.

counts.title: Counts
counts.description: How many counted requirements have each verification status; indirect apart from verified; they add up to total.

open.title: Open
open.description: Requirements with the verification status open.

verified.title: Verified
verified.description: Requirements with the verification status verified.

indirect.title: Indirect
indirect.description: Requirements verified indirectly, through their children.

failed.title: Failed
failed.description: Requirements with the verification status failed.

outdated.title: Outdated
outdated.description: Requirements with the verification status outdated.

schemas.title: Element file frontmatter
schemas.description: YAML frontmatter of an element file. The Markdown text follows the closing `---`. Only `id`, `type` and `status` are structural (`status` only for a type with statuses); every other key is a property or relation kind key from the metamodel. Keys the metamodel does not know are kept unchanged and reported as hints. See docs/adr/0004-element-file-format.md. File name: type prefix, dash, last 12 hex characters of the UUID, never changed. Value kinds are checked against the metamodel, not by this schema, so any value of an unknown key is kept; `$defs/value` describes the values ReqSeq writes.

type.description: Type key from the metamodel.

status.description: Status key from the metamodel, one of the statuses of the element's type. Left out for a type without status. Only ever set by a person.

normal-form.description: Reserved. Never written; the normal-form version is part of every stored version string.

criterion.description: An acceptance criterion with its criterion key, as the element file stores it: a block mapping, key first. Only in the list of the property with the meaning acceptance-criteria; the key never counts to the version.

key.description: The criterion key: a lower-case letter a to z, then 3 to 15 lower-case letters a to z or digits; unique in the requirement and kept while the criterion exists.

text.description: The text of the acceptance criterion, Markdown.

key.description: Its key.

inputValue.description: Property value of a write command: like `value`, but a relation target is an element reference (UUID, short ID or identifier, alone or as `{ id, repository? }`) whose version ReqSeq sets.

value.description: Property value (text, number, date as YYYY-MM-DD, choice key, list) or relation targets. Which one is expected comes from the metamodel; a mismatch is a hint, not a parse error.

schemas.title: Evidence record, Markdown frontmatter
schemas.description: Open format for a verification or validation record. A manual record is a Markdown file with this frontmatter; the text below may describe the check. Automatic test results stay JUnit XML; the same fields are JUnit properties, see docs/adr/0012-evidence-records.md. The evidence itself stays where it is; `evidence` only points to it. Records written by ReqSeq and by anyone else count the same.

kind.description: Verification or validation. Validation counts only for the validation status.

element.description: Verification: a requirement. Validation: a need or a requirement.

variant.description: Variant the record holds for. Absent: the core, and also every variant the element applies in when the element's repository is marked `variant-independent` in the workspace file. Verification only: a validation record with a variant is refused and counts for no status.

item.description: The item under test: the concrete build or sample that was checked. Required for verification, optional for validation.

reason.description: The reason for an `inconclusive` validation, at least one character that is not white space; required with `inconclusive` and only there. A reader warns about it on another result and reads the record without it.

evidence.description: Where the evidence document is: relative path, file URL or any URI. ReqSeq does not open or manage it.

test-case.description: Optional test case name or ID.

criteria.description: The acceptance criteria the record holds for, each by its criterion key or by its number: the position in the property with the meaning `acceptance-criteria` of the element's `version`, counted from 1. `evidence.record` writes keys. The record counts for the criterion of the current version with that key; a number of an older version counts through the key the criterion had in the newest commit with that version. Absent: every criterion. Verification only: a reader warns about it on a validation record, which counts per element, and reads the record without it. A key that no criterion of the named version carries, or a number that version does not have, is a problem of `workspace check` (`evidence.unknown-criterion`).

schemas.title: Saved filter file
schemas.description: A named filter saved as YAML in the repository: a `*.yaml` file directly in the `filters` folder of the workspace file. The same condition language is the `where` of every command that takes a selection, so a saved filter gives the same elements in app, CLI, API and MCP. Element references may take any form (`resolveRef`); `filter.save` writes UUIDs.

description.description: What the filter is for, for people.

view.description: Elements that apply in this view; also the view of its `verification` conditions without `variant`.

sort.description: Order of `element.list` when its input gives no `sort`.

name.description: Name of a saved filter, unique in the workspace ignoring case; used to call it (`selection.filter`). Saving under an existing name replaces that filter.

condition.description: Combinable condition. Exactly one operator per object. `all`: every condition holds (`[]` holds), `any`: some holds (`[]` does not), `not`: it does not hold.

all.title: All of
all.description: Conditions that must all hold; `[]` holds.

any.title: Any of
any.description: Conditions of which at least one must hold; `[]` does not.

type.title: Types
type.description: Type keys; an element of a subtype matches too unless `subtypes` is false.

subtypes.title: With subtypes
subtypes.description: Include subtypes of the type. Absent means true.

status.title: Statuses
status.description: Status keys as written in the files.

validFor.title: Valid for
validFor.description: Elements that apply in this view by their validity only, not the view: replacements and exclusions do not count.

verification.title: Verification status
verification.description: Verification status in `variant`, else in the view of the selection, else in the core.

variant.title: Variant
variant.description: View the verification status is computed in. Absent: the view of the selection, else the core.

validation.title: Validation status
validation.description: Needs always (open without record), requirements only with a validation record, no other element.

emergent.title: Emergent
emergent.description: true: the property with the meaning `emergent` is `yes`; false: it is not.

source.title: Source
source.description: Value of the property with meaning `source` of imported elements.

text.title: Text search
text.description: Elements that element.search finds for this query in all fields: every word in the title, text, a property value, the type or status name, or an ID, typo tolerant, in any case, also as a word start, and, exact with 4+ letters and no digit, inside words, quoted words as a phrase, a designation through its element's other ones, criterion keys and references. A query without a word matches none.

conditionStub.description: Only in MCP tools other than `element_search`, never in a saved filter file: a filter condition (`condition`); its grammar is in the input schema of `element_search`, under `selection.where`.

propertyCondition.description: Condition on the values of any property: none when it is absent, `null` or `[]`, else the items of a list or the one value. `exists`: some value, `missing`: none (both without `value`). `eq`: some value equals `value` (1 is not "1"), `ne`: not `eq`, `in`: some value equals an item of the list `value`. `contains`: some text contains `value`, ignoring case. `lt`, `le`, `gt`, `ge`: numbers with numbers, texts with texts by code units (ISO dates compare as dates). `matches`: some text matches the JavaScript regular expression `value` (flag u). A choice may be given by its display name. A key that holds relations takes element references, with `eq`, `ne`, `in`, `exists` and `missing` only.

op.title: Comparison
op.description: The comparison, as the condition describes it.

value.title: Value
value.description: The value to compare with; a list for `in`; none for `exists` and `missing`.

relationCondition.description: Condition on relations, e.g. without child: {relation: {meaning: derivation, direction: down}, exists: false}. Evidence is a relation direction too. `exists: true` without `to` counts a relation also when its target is not available; with `to`, only an available other end that meets it.

kind.title: Relation kind
kind.description: A relation kind or a property of kind relation (validity, packages); with `meaning`, the kind must have it.

meaning.title: Meaning
meaning.description: Every relation kind with this meaning. Neither `kind` nor `meaning`: every relation kind.

direction.title: Direction
direction.description: `up` = outgoing (to parents), `down` = incoming (from children), `evidence` = verification records pointing at the element in the view of the selection, else in the core (a record without variant holds for the core, and for every variant when the element's repository is marked `variant-independent`; one with a variant for that variant), of any version and result; validation records do not count; no `kind`, `meaning` or `to`. Absent: up or down.

to.title: To
to.description: Condition the other end must meet.

exists.title: Exists
exists.description: `true`: the element has such a relation. `false`: it has none.

sortKey.description: A sort key; no order is stored in element files.

by.title: Sort by
by.description: `id`: short ID. `identifier`: the property with the meaning `identifier`, digit runs by number (SR-9 before SR-10), else short ID after; `desc` reverses both. `type`, `status`: metamodel order. `title`: the title property. `verification`: verification status in the selection's view (else core): failed, open, outdated, verified (`indirect` too). `versionDate`: version time; uncommitted is newest. `hierarchy`: the derivation tree, ascending only. Else a property key the metamodel or an element has (no relations), by its first value: choices in metamodel order, then numbers, texts (ignoring case), booleans; no value last in both orders.

schemas.title: HTML export marker file
schemas.description: The file `reqseq-html-export.yaml` that `html.export` writes into the folder of an HTML export: it lists the files that export wrote, so the next export into the same folder replaces or removes exactly those and leaves every other file as it is. A folder that is not empty and holds no such file is never written into. ReqSeq writes it anew on every export; it is not meant to be edited.

files.description: The files of the export, relative to its folder, with `/`, sorted by code units. An entry that names no file the export may replace (`..`, an absolute path, a name `.git` or a nested repository on its way, a symbolic link) is neither replaced nor removed.

pending.description: Only while an export runs: the folder `.reqseq-export-staging` it writes into before the files go into place. An export that finds it left by a process that no longer runs removes it.

schemas.title: Metamodel file
schemas.description: One YAML file of the metamodel. A metamodel is all *.yaml files in the metamodel folder named in the workspace file; their lists are merged, and every key must be unique across all files. Keys never change; names may. Built-in meanings are attached with `meaning`. A type or property meaning is assigned to at most one key, counting only the `meaning` a definition sets itself and would not inherit anyway; a second key is a metamodel error; several relation kinds may share a relation meaning, e.g. Refines and Derives from are both `derivation`. A type inherits the meaning of the type it extends unless it sets its own.

prefix.description: Prefix of a short ID: upper case letters and digits, starting with a letter.

name.title: Name
name.description: Display name. English in the standard model.

type.description: Element type.

prefix.title: Prefix
prefix.description: Prefix of the short ID, e.g. SR. UNKNOWN is reserved for elements of an unknown type and is a metamodel error.

extends.title: Extends
extends.description: Parent type; its properties and required properties are inherited, over any number of levels. A parent that is not defined, or a cycle, is a metamodel error.

abstract.title: Abstract
abstract.description: No elements of this type can be created; only for inheritance.

properties.title: Properties
properties.description: Property keys this type has, in addition to inherited ones, which come first. Each should be a defined property; an undefined key is a metamodel warning and the type is treated as not having it.

required.title: Required properties
required.description: Mandatory property keys, in addition to inherited ones; each is also a property of the type and should be a defined property; an undefined key is a metamodel warning and the type is treated as not having it. Empty values are allowed but give a hint.

statuses.title: Statuses
statuses.description: Status keys elements of this type may have, in addition to inherited ones: the top-level `statuses` stay the vocabulary (names, `invalid`, `initial`), a type only restricts it. Left out on the type and on every ancestor: every status. Once the type or any ancestor has a list, only the listed statuses count: a type with a list below a parent without one has only its own statuses (an unrestricted parent does not add every status). An empty list on a type whose ancestors have none: the type has no status, and its element files have no `status`. Each should be a defined status; an undefined key is a metamodel warning and left out (when no key is left, the type has no status). A type whose statuses are all marked invalid (e.g. `[retired]`) has an optional status: its elements without status are current, element.create gives them none, and element.supersede retires them. A status outside the list gives a hint on the element (`element.status-not-allowed`).

typeMeaning.description: Built-in meaning of the type: `requirement` (target of verification), `need` (always has a validation status, open without records), `variant`, `package`.

effectiveType.description: A type with its inheritance resolved, as metamodel.get returns it; never written in a file. Key, name, description, prefix and extends are as written in the type's definition.

name.title: Name
name.description: Display name of the type.

description.title: Description
description.description: What the type means, for people.

abstract.title: Abstract
abstract.description: Not inherited: a type is abstract only when its own definition says so.

ancestors.title: Ancestor types
ancestors.description: The parent, its parent and so on, up to the root type.

properties.title: Properties
properties.description: All property keys of the type, each once: those of the root type first, then down to the type itself (the key order of new keys in element files). Required keys count as properties. Keys that no property definition has are left out.

required.title: Required properties
required.description: All required property keys, own and inherited, in the same order. Keys that no property definition has are left out.

statuses.title: Statuses
statuses.description: The status keys elements of the type may have, own and inherited, in the order of the metamodel's statuses: every status when neither the type nor an ancestor has `statuses`; empty when the type has no status. Keys that no status definition has are left out.

meaning.title: Meaning
meaning.description: Own meaning, else the meaning of the closest ancestor that has one.

property.description: Property definition. Its key is not `id`, `type` or `status`, the fields every element has; such a key is a metamodel error.

kind.title: Value kind
kind.description: Value kind.

target-types.title: Target types
target-types.description: Allowed target types, for kind `relation`: absent: every type; empty: none; a type also allows its subtypes (types that extend it).

content.title: Part of the version
content.description: Part of the content and therefore of the version. Title and status are never content.

markdown.title: Markdown
markdown.description: Values are Markdown like the text: emphasis, code and inline references `[label](reqseq:<uuid>?version=...)`, which are followed, checked and confirmed like those in the text. Only for kind `text`, and never with the meaning `title` or `identifier`. It does not change the version of an element; images in such a value are no embedded images.

max-items.title: Maximum entries
max-items.description: At most this many entries in the list: an element with more is the hint `element.too-many-items` when the workspace is checked, never a refusal. Only with `many: true` and not for kind `relation`. Absent: any number.

propertyMeaning.description: Built-in meaning: `title`; `validity` (list of variants); `packages`; `emergent` (emergent behaviour; a choice without `many` whose key `yes` is the mark; otherwise a warning and nothing is marked); `verification-method`; `statement` (the statement for ReqIF); `source`, `source-identifier`, `import-date`, `delivery`, `import-version` (origin of imported elements, written only by ReqIF import; `import-version` is the import version, the version of what the import wrote, right after the last import, kind `text` without `many` and never `content`); `identifier` (an ID people read and name besides the UUID, from another source or by a running scheme of the project, such as the spec ID SR-036 or a customer ID; unique per type; `element.create` with `nextIdentifier` gives the one after the highest of the type with the same identifier prefix; element references accept it besides the UUID and short ID, and outputs show it next to the short ID). A property with the meaning `identifier` is of kind `text` without `many`. `acceptance-criteria` (the acceptance criteria of a requirement, counted from 1 in their order, which evidence records name by criterion key or by number; kind `text` with `many`, otherwise a warning and no criterion is read). `synonyms` (designations of the element with the same meaning; kind `text` with `many`, otherwise a warning) and `translation` (the element's designation in another language; kind `text`, otherwise a warning); the designations of an element are its title, its synonyms and its translation.

relationKind.description: Relation kind. Stored under its key in the source file, which is not `id`, `type` or `status`, the fields every element has (such a key is a metamodel error). `source-types`/`target-types` restrict where it may be set.

inverse-name.title: Inverse name
inverse-name.description: Name shown at the target, e.g. Derived by.

source-types.title: Source types
source-types.description: Allowed source types: absent: every type; empty: none; a type also allows its subtypes (types that extend it).

target-types.title: Target types
target-types.description: Allowed target types: absent: every type; empty: none; a type also allows its subtypes (types that extend it).

limits.title: Limits
limits.description: How many relations of this kind an element may or must have, per target type: a count outside a limit is a hint (`relation.too-many`, `relation.too-few`) when the workspace is checked, never a refusal. Absent: any number, also none. One limit per pair of source type and target type.

relationLimit.description: A minimum, a maximum or both for the number of relations of the kind from one source element to elements of `target-type`. Both types include their subtypes (types that extend them). A relation counts when its target resolves to one element of a known type; a duplicate item counts twice.

source-type.title: Source type
source-type.description: The source elements the limit applies to. Absent: the kind's `source-types`, or every type when the kind has none.

target-type.title: Target type
target-type.description: The type of the targets that are counted.

min.title: Minimum
min.description: At least this many relations; fewer is the hint `relation.too-few`.

max.title: Maximum
max.description: At most this many relations; more is the hint `relation.too-many`.

relationMeaning.description: Built-in meaning. `derivation`: source is child, target is parent (chain, coverage, indirect verification). `replacement`: source replaces target core requirement for the variants in the source's validity. `succession`: source is the successor that supersedes target. `exclusion`: source variant excludes target core requirement, written in the variant file. Without meaning a relation has no traceability semantics.

status.description: Status value.

invalid.title: Invalid
invalid.description: Elements with this status do not count for coverage and indirect verification, but stay visible in chains.

initial.title: Initial
initial.description: Status of new elements. Exactly one status is initial. A type whose statuses do not include it gives its new elements its first status that is not marked invalid, in metamodel order, and so does every type when the initial status is marked invalid (a metamodel warning); a type without status or with only invalid statuses gives them none.

schemas.title: Perspective file
schemas.description: A perspective saved as YAML in the repository: a list of elements with a name, its selection, its grouping and its sort, as a `*.yaml` file directly in the `perspectives` folder of the workspace file. A perspective stores no view; the view comes from `selection.view`. Element references may take any form; `perspective.save` writes UUIDs.

description.description: What the perspective is for, for people.

filter.description: Name of a saved filter that the selection also uses, read again on each call.

where.description: The conditions of the selection, in the language of a saved filter. A selection with no condition is `{ all: [] }`.

group.description: The grouping of the list. Absent: not grouped.

name.description: Name of a perspective, unique among the perspectives of the workspace ignoring case and Unicode normal form; a saved filter may have the same name. Saving under an existing name replaces that perspective.

schemas.title: Recent workspaces file
schemas.description: `recent-workspaces.json` in `<OS cache>/reqseq/`: the workspaces opened last, the most recent first, at most 20, one per folder. `workspace.markOpened` records the root of the workspace it runs on, and `workspace.recent` reads the list. It is private (mode 0600, like `api.json`), holds absolute paths of the user's workspaces and nothing else, and lies outside every working tree. Removing it only forgets the list.

workspaces.description: The most recent first; no two entries with the same `key`.

workspace.description: One workspace that was opened: its root, its canonical name and when it was opened last.

root.description: The absolute path of the workspace root as it was opened last (the folder that holds `reqseq-workspace.yaml`); shown, and opened as it is.

key.description: The canonical root (absolute, symbolic links resolved, lower case on Windows), computed when the workspace was opened: two names of one folder are one entry. Never resolved again on reading.

schemas.title: ReqIF mapping file
schemas.description: Mapping of the types and attributes of one ReqIF source to the own metamodel, saved as YAML in the mapping folder of the workspace (`mappings`, default `reqif` in the main repository) and reused for every later import from and export to that source. The own metamodel is never changed by it. Also holds saved export profiles and the source's own model, which the imports through it gather so an export can write in that model.

settings.description: The keys of a mapping but `source-model`: what `reqif.saveMapping` takes, since only `reqif.import` writes the source model.

source.description: The ReqIF source this mapping is for.

name.description: Name of the source as written to the property with meaning `source`.

tool-id.description: REQ-IF-TOOL-ID seen in deliveries, for recognising the source.

target.description: Folder where imported elements are written.

types.description: Each SPEC-OBJECT-TYPE of the source, mapped to a type or omitted.

source.description: LONG-NAME or IDENTIFIER of the SPEC-OBJECT-TYPE.

omit.description: Objects of this type are not imported; each is listed as a loss.

attributes.description: Each ATTRIBUTE-DEFINITION of the source, mapped to the title, the text or a property, or omitted.

source-type.description: Restricts the entry to one SPEC-OBJECT-TYPE.

source.description: LONG-NAME or IDENTIFIER of the ATTRIBUTE-DEFINITION.

property.description: Where the value goes: `title`, `text` or the key of a property.

omit-values.description: Enumeration values left out on import, each listed as a loss.

omit.description: The attribute is not imported, which is listed as a loss.

relations.description: Each SPEC-RELATION-TYPE of the source, mapped to a relation kind or omitted.

source.description: LONG-NAME or IDENTIFIER of the SPEC-RELATION-TYPE.

omit.description: Relations of this type are not imported.

statement.description: Where the statement goes when exporting back to the source.

property.description: Own property that holds the statement.

datatype.description: How the statement is written: as STRING, or as XHTML converted from its Markdown.

omit-properties.description: Properties left out of every export to this source; written by `reqif.export` with `mapping` and `omitProperties`.

export-profiles.description: Saved exports to this source, each a selection under a name.

name.description: Name of the profile.

omit-properties.description: Properties left out of every export with this profile.

sourceModel.description: The source's own model, so an export can write in it, gathered by the imports through this mapping: the SPEC-OBJECT-TYPEs they mapped to a type, with their ATTRIBUTE-DEFINITIONs and the datatypes these use, each with IDENTIFIER and LONG-NAME and every facet as written in the file. Each import replaces the types of the `types` entries it delivers and keeps the others. Written only by `reqif.import` with `mapping`, never for a file of ReqSeq; `reqif.saveMapping` keeps it, unless `file` replaces the mapping of another source.

datatypes.description: The datatypes the attributes of `types` use.

long-name.description: Its LONG-NAME, when the file has one.

kind.description: Which DATATYPE-DEFINITION it is.

max-length.description: MAX-LENGTH of a STRING, as written.

min.description: MIN of an INTEGER or REAL, as written.

max.description: MAX of an INTEGER or REAL, as written.

accuracy.description: ACCURACY of a REAL, as written.

values.description: SPECIFIED-VALUES of an ENUMERATION, in the file's order.

long-name.description: Its LONG-NAME, when the file has one.

key.description: KEY of its EMBEDDED-VALUE, as written.

other-content.description: OTHER-CONTENT of its EMBEDDED-VALUE, as written.

types.description: The SPEC-OBJECT-TYPEs an import through this mapping mapped to a type, also those no `types` entry maps any more.

long-name.description: Its LONG-NAME, when the file has one.
