attributes.description: Its ATTRIBUTE-DEFINITIONs, in the file's order, mapped or omitted.

long-name.description: Its LONG-NAME, when the file has one.

datatype.description: IDENTIFIER of its datatype, an entry of `datatypes`.

multi-valued.description: MULTI-VALUED of an enumeration attribute; left out when false.

schemas.title: Local workspace overrides
schemas.description: `.reqseq/local.yaml` next to `reqseq-workspace.yaml`: settings of one person on one machine. A file Git tracks or has staged is ignored with a warning, and the places of the workspace file apply; `workspace.init` adds `.reqseq/local.yaml` to `.gitignore`. It overrides where a repository of the workspace lies locally. Faulty content is reported as a warning and ignored.

repositories.description: Per repository name of the workspace file: where it lies on this machine.

path.description: Absolute path, or relative to the main repository (the folder with `reqseq-workspace.yaml`). No `~` expansion.

schemas.title: Workspace file
schemas.description: `reqseq-workspace.yaml` in the root of the main repository. Names the repositories that belong together. Everyone has locally only those they may access; missing ones are shown as not available. A single-repository workspace lists only itself.

name.description: Name of the workspace.

repositories.description: The entry with `main: true` is the repository that holds this file. With two or more repositories exactly one has `main: true`; a single repository is the main one even without it. Names are unique (checked by ReqSeq; JSON Schema cannot express it).

metamodel.description: Where the metamodel lies: a folder in one of the repositories, the main one or its own.

evidence.description: Folders with evidence records (Markdown) and JUnit XML files. They may be in repositories of other tools.

baselines.description: Where new baseline files are written. Default: folder `baselines` in the main repository.

filters.description: Where saved filters are written. Default: folder `filters` in the main repository.

perspectives.description: Where perspectives are written. Default: folder `perspectives` in the main repository.

mappings.description: Where ReqIF mapping files are written. Default: folder `reqif` in the main repository.

ignore.description: Glob patterns of paths that are never read as elements, relative to each repository and anchored at its root, with `/` as separator (no `\`, no `//`). `*` matches any characters within one name, `?` one character, `**` as a whole name any number of names, including none; every other character is literal (no `[...]`, no `{a,b}`). Case-sensitive on every OS; wildcards match names starting with `.`. A leading `/` or `./` and a trailing `/` are dropped; `x/**` matches folder `x` itself, so it is skipped as a whole. Example: `website/**`, `**/*.draft.md`. `.git` and `node_modules` are always ignored.

name.description: Name of the repository in the workspace: lower case letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`.

url.description: Address of the repository on the Git server. Informational: ReqSeq never clones or fetches.

path.description: Expected local location relative to the main repository, with `/` as separator. Default `../<name>`; always `.` for the main repository. Absolute paths and `\` are warned about; an absolute path is ignored, and so is one that leaves the folder holding the main repository or passes a link out of a repository (it can lead to a network share); there is no `~` expansion. A person can override it in the untracked file `.reqseq/local.yaml`.

main.description: The repository that holds this file.

variant-independent.description: The repository does not know the variants of the workspace: an evidence record without `variant` for one of its elements counts in the core and in every variant the element applies in (the view rule). Without the mark such a record counts only in the core. Shared: `.reqseq/local.yaml` cannot change it. An older ReqSeq rejects a workspace file with it (`file.faulty`).

main.description: The repository that holds this file.

repository.title: Repository
repository.description: Workspace name of the repository.

name.description: group.action; CLI `reqseq group action`, API `POST /v1/commands/group.action`, MCP tool `group_action`.

title.description: The name of the command for people, English, sentence case, unique in the catalog: the MCP tool `title`. Free of delete words except for relations and for entries with `deletes`.

summary.description: What the command does and what for, in one or two sentences in the user's words: the command reference, its index, `--help`, the MCP tool description and the OpenAPI summary show it. At most 50 words, counted as the text split at white space (`catalog-checks.mjs`).

details.description: What a user needs to know beyond the summary: rules, cases and limits of the command. Shown on the command's reference page below the summary, not in the index, `--help` or the MCP tool list. Implementation notes belong in the block files of `packages/core/docs/`.

effect.description: No command writes to Git. No command deletes elements; only entries with `deletes` delete a file.

whileReadOnly.description: Whether a `write-files` command runs while the workspace is read-only (a missing or faulty metamodel): `refuse` gives `workspace.read-only` before the command runs, `allow` runs it (`workspace.init`, which creates the workspace). Required for `write-files`, not allowed for `read` (reads always run). Each command's SR decides; until then `refuse`.

whileReadOnlyReason.description: Why the command has its `whileReadOnly` value, in one line for the people who change it. Required with `whileReadOnly`.

deletes.description: The command deletes a file, the file of a perspective or saved filter, which is no element: only with a boolean `confirm` input whose default is false (`catalog-checks.mjs`). Allowed only on `write-files` entries of the groups `perspective` and `filter`. It allows delete words in the name and title and sets the MCP `destructiveHint`.

loadUpfront.description: The command is on the everyday path of an agent: the MCP server marks its tool with `_meta["anthropic/alwaysLoad"]: true`, so a client that defers tools loads this one with its schema at once. Left out on every other command; other accesses ignore it.

stage.description: The stage in which the command is built.

arguments.description: How a command prompt asks for the input: every top-level property of `input` exactly once, the required ones first, in the order they are asked. `complete` says where the values to offer come from (a closed list; `folder` and `file` map to `workspace.listFolder`, because only `@reqseq/core` reads the file system, and `searchField` to `element.searchFields`: the read commands made for completion). `of` names an earlier field the source depends on. Without it, the nearest earlier field of the fitting source, never an `element` field with a `meaning`: an `element` or `relationTarget` field for status, invalidStatus, relationKind, hint, property and relation (relation also a `relation` field); an `element` field for criterion and elementFile; a `relationKind` field for relationTarget; a `property` field for value; a `type` field for properties and relations; a `folder` field for metamodelLocation. With no such field, status, invalidStatus, relationKind, hint and property give every value of the metamodel or the workspace; the others need one. `validate-schemas.mjs` checks the coverage, the order, `of` and the fields each source fits (`catalog-checks.mjs`).

complete.description: element: elements found by element.search; with `meaning`, the elements of the types with that meaning (metamodel.get, then element.list), as view offers the variants, without `core`. type: types of the metamodel. status: statuses of the type of the element in `of` (without it, every status of the metamodel). invalidStatus: of those, the ones the metamodel marks invalid. relationKind: kinds that relation.options allows from the element in `of` (without it, every relation kind of the metamodel). relationTarget: elements of the target types of the kind in `of` (element.search with selection.where.type). relation: with `of` an element field, the kinds of the existing relations of that element; with `of` a relation field (the kind asked before), the targets of the relations of that kind (relation.remove: source, kind, target). property: properties of the type of the element in `of` (every property of the metamodel without it). value: the values the metamodel fixes for the property in `of`. hint: open hints of the element in `of` (without it, every open hint). filter: saved filters. baseline: baselines (baseline.list). perspective: perspectives (perspective.list). view: `core` and the variants of the workspace (element.list of the types with the meaning `variant`). repository: repositories of the workspace. selection: the selection of the list shown. choice: the `enum` of the property or of its items, inline or in the definition its `$ref` names (`hint.list` `kind`: the problem codes of `common.schema.json`). folder: a `localPath` field that names a folder, file: one that names a file; both completed with the entries of the typed folder (workspace.listFolder, files only for file), and every `localPath` field has one of them (`catalog-checks.mjs`). criterion: the acceptance criteria of the element in `of` (element.get `criterionReferences`), each by its key; a criterion without a key is not offered, since evidence.record refuses it. evidenceLocation: the evidence locations of the workspace (workspace.status `evidence[].folder`); evidence.record refuses one while the repository of the location is not on this machine; typed text stays, for a folder below one. elementFile: the file of the element in `of` (element.get), or, when the reference is ambiguous, the files of the elements it names (`details.candidates` of `ref.ambiguous`, the answer of the same read command). metamodelLocation: an object `{ repository?, path }`, asked in two steps: the repository (the main repository the default), then the path (in the main repository the folders below the folder in `of`, workspace.listFolder; typed text accepted). group: a `groupKey` field: `type`, `status`, `package` (when the meaning `packages` is assigned) and the properties element.facets gives values for. Composed values, each one flat entry whose field's schema fixes the parts (`catalog-checks.mjs` binds them): condition: a `condition` field of `filter.schema.json`, built from parts: types, statuses and properties with their values (metamodel.get, element.facets over the conditions chosen before), verification and validation status (their enums), validity (core and the variants, as view), relations (the relation kinds of metamodel.get and the `relationCondition` enums) and text. sort: a list of `sortKey`: the keys of its `by` enum and the metamodel.get properties that hold no relations, each with an order from its enum. searchField: a list of `searchFieldKey` (element.search `fields`): the fields element.searchFields lists, each by its name with its key beside. properties: an object of `inputValue` by property key: the properties of the type in `of` (metamodel.get) without the title and those given, each value as value gives it. relations: a `relationRefs` field: the kinds metamodel.get `relationKinds` gives for the type in `of`, then elements of their target types (element.search). choices: a list of new fixed values `{ name, key? }`, each a name and its key, the key suggested from the name. choiceChanges: a list of `{ choice, name?, description? }`: a fixed value of the property (metamodel.get), then its new name or description. limits: a list of `relationLimit` of metamodel.schema.json: the target types for limits as marks from every type (metamodel.get; those of the limits there are marked, a limit for one source type is kept as it is), then a minimum and a maximum, each a number or empty, per target type marked. text, number, boolean: typed free input; in the steps of the metamodel commands, an empty input of a `number` field that also takes null gives null. json: any other object or mixed field, typed as JSON and checked by `@reqseq/core`.

meaning.description: Only on an `element` source: the field takes an element whose type has this meaning (`variant`; `package`), and its values are those elements. A field with a meaning is never the nearest earlier field a source without `of` reads, so `evidence.record criteria` reads `ref`, not `variant`; an explicit `of` may name it (`catalog-checks.mjs`).

class.description: Required on a `text` source and only there (`catalog-checks.mjs`): what the free text is, from a closed list, so a new text argument is taken up on purpose. name, title, text, description: a name, a title, a text or a description; time: a point in time; version: a version of an element; revision: a Git revision; query: a search query or a pattern that finds text; path: a path or another location of a file; output: a value another command gives, such as the plan of a preview of element.bulkUpdate or the content of an attachment. Numbers are `number` sources; as JSON the command prompt asks only the mapping of reqif.saveMapping (a `json` source); keys and prefixes of new metamodel definitions are `name`.

replaces.description: Earlier optional fields a value of this field takes the place of: the prompt leaves them out of the input when this field has a value other than `false`, so they only said what it offers. `hint.confirm`: hints chosen at `hintIds` confirm only those, not every hint `ref`, `target` and `kind` select; `all` yes confirms those of the workspace, not those of the shown element as `ref`. `catalog-checks.mjs` checks the fields.

flag.description: Name of the CLI flag, without `--`, when it is not the field name in kebab-case: `element.create` takes its `properties` as `--set key=value`, as `element.update` takes `set`. Not the name of another field's flag, nor of a common option (`validate-schemas.mjs`, `catalog-checks.mjs`).

items.description: A top-level array of `output`: one line per item.

fields.description: Top-level fields of `output` that every line carries before the keys of its item, in this order; a field the output leaves out is left out of the lines too. None is an array or a property of the item schema (`catalog-checks.mjs`).

jsonLines.description: The command also gives its output as JSON Lines (one compact JSON object and LF per line, UTF-8): the CLI with `--jsonl`, the API with `Accept: application/x-ndjson`. Each line is the listed `fields` of the output, then one item of `items`; the other top-level fields are not in the lines. MCP keeps the JSON object.

outputFields.description: Written by `generate.mjs` into the generated catalog only, never in a command file: every field of `output`, also those inside shared definitions, with its title and marks resolved from the definitions, so a reader needs no `$ref`. A definition already on the way to a field is not entered again.

path.description: The field, from the root of the output: `levels[].elements.withChildren`, `[]` for the items of an array, `*` for the keys of a map.

title.description: The title of the field for people.

technical.description: The value is technical (a UUID, path, check value, commit, kind of a problem or duration) and shown only on request; `with-element`: only when the same problem names an element.

normal.description: The normal value: a shown value equal to it appears only with Show details.

elements.description: `answer`: the elements that are the answer of the output. `true`: listed elements. A list of paths: the lists of the elements this number counts. `selection`: a number of elements of a read command that only `element.list` lists, with `selection.output.count`.

keys.description: Only for a number of elements: for each list it is in (each `[]` of `path`, outermost first), the fields of an entry that identify it (`x-key`); `selection.output.count.key` gives one object of these fields per list. A field an entry does not have is left out of the object.

textOutput.description: A required top-level `string` field of `output` (`catalog-checks.mjs`) that is the command's text: the CLI prints exactly this string to stdout without `--json` or `--yaml`, and the problems alone to stderr. API and MCP keep the JSON object.

output.description: Outputs are JSON objects and say so at the root, also next to a `$ref`: MCP needs `type: object` at the root of an output schema.

catalog.description: The command catalog: one file per command, schemas/commands/<name>.json, in the order of schemas/commands/catalog.header.json. Every function of ReqSeq is one command here. CLI, API, MCP server and app are generated from these files; schemas/generated/ is derived and checked in CI. A change to a command file is a contract change, announced in the milestone epic.

commands.name: workspace.init
commands.title: Create workspace
commands.summary: Create a workspace with the standard model in a folder, which is created when only it is missing, with the folder `evidence` as its evidence location, and write the skill file for AI agents. Adds `*.reqseq-tmp` (temp files of an interrupted write) to the folder's `.gitignore`.
commands.details: The skill file is written as `tool.guide` with `skill` and `write` writes it, without `replace`, at each of its places: `.claude/skills/managing-requirements/SKILL.md` and `.agents/skills/managing-requirements/SKILL.md` in the root of the Git repository of the folder, or in the folder without Git. Each place written is listed in `files`. ReqSeq's own unchanged file of another version is left as it is and not listed. A file at a place that ReqSeq did not write, or that was changed since, is kept, and one problem `workspace.skill-not-written` per place not written says where and why; the other place is written all the same, and the workspace is created all the same. `skill: false` writes no skill file. commands.name: tool.guide
commands.title: Agent guide
commands.summary: The guide for an AI agent that works with ReqSeq: the steps from need to verification degree with the command of each step, the rules, and the types, statuses and evidence locations of this workspace. On request it gives the skill file or the MCP server instructions instead.
commands.details: The text is the same in every access for the same input. `names` chooses whether commands appear as command-line calls or as MCP tool names; the calls for a pipeline are always command-line calls. Without a workspace, or with a metamodel that cannot be read, the guide leaves out the facts of the metamodel and says why; without a workspace it names the call that creates one. With `skill`, the output is the skill file `managing-requirements` in the format of Agent Skills: the workflows as numbered steps, each command as MCP tool and command-line call, no name of the metamodel, and the version of ReqSeq and a checksum in its frontmatter. With `write`, it is written at two places, in this order, each on its own: `.claude/skills/managing-requirements/SKILL.md`, where Claude Code looks, and `.agents/skills/managing-requirements/SKILL.md`, where other clients look, both in the root of the Git repository of the workspace folder, or in the workspace folder without Git. At each place, a file that ReqSeq did not write, or that was changed since, is replaced only with `replace`, which holds for every place. Through the API and the MCP server, a place outside the repositories of the workspace is refused with the command-line call that writes the file. A folder `.agents/skills` linked to `.claude/skills` inside the repository finds the file the first place wrote, so the second place is `unchanged`; a link at `SKILL.md` itself is refused. When a place is not written, the other places are written all the same and the call fails: the error has the code of the first place not written, names each place with its result, and lists them in `details.places`. With `instructions`, the output is what the MCP server sends as its instructions: the title of the guide, a paragraph that says to read the guide with `tool_guide` before the first step, and the rules section with MCP tool names; it reads nothing from the folder, so it is the same with or without a workspace, and is at most 4,000 characters long. `instructions` and `skill` cannot be given together.

The calls for a pipeline stay command-line calls. Ignored with `skill`, which names every command both ways, and with `instructions`, which names every command as MCP tool.

commands.name: metamodel.addType
commands.title: Add type
commands.summary: Add an element type to the metamodel; only the metamodel file that gets it changes, line by line.
commands.details: The type is added at the end of `types` in the first metamodel file by name that has the list, else at the end of the first file, where the list is created. Every other line of the file stays as it was, with its comment and line ending; no element file changes and nothing in Git. Without `key`, the key is made from the name: lower case, the German umlauts and sharp s as ae, oe, ue and ss, other letters with a diacritic as the letter without it (é as e), every run of other characters one hyphen; it is fixed afterwards. ref.description: UUID, short ID or identifier of the element, any case; or the reference to one of its acceptance criteria as a test name writes it: `[SR-036/AK-k7f3]`, or `SR-036/AK-k7f3` without brackets, split at the first `/` as enrich-junit reads it. A bracket token without such a suffix or with another one (`[SR-036]`, `[SR-036/slow]`) names the element. A suffix that names a criterion by its number (`AK` and a number) is refused with input.invalid and `details.reason` `criterion-by-number`, as test names name criteria by key; one that tries to name a criterion in another form (`AK-x`, or the number 0) with `details.reason` `criterion-malformed`.

version.description: The version the reference stores; optional. A version of normal form n1 or n2 is compared with the current version in its own form; a version of another normal form is refused with input.invalid.

versionDate.description: Also give the date of the current version (`versionDate`), read from the Git history, as element.get does with the same input. Without it no git runs and `versionDate` is left out.

repository.description: Which of the elements ref names is meant: the workspace name of its repository, as details.candidates of ref.ambiguous give it (for example one copy of a file whose UUID another file shares). Only the elements ref names count; when none of them lies there, the error is ref.unknown with them as details.candidates.

file.description: Which of the elements ref names is meant: its file, relative to its repository, as details.candidates of ref.ambiguous give it. Give repository too when the same path is in several repositories; when several elements are still left, the error is ref.ambiguous with them.

element.title: Element
element.description: The element as element.get shows it, with title, text, status, current version in normal form n2, verification status per view it is in and validation status and, with the input `versionDate`, the date of that version (as element.get gives it; left out without the input). Without a version (a value that counts has no normal form) `version` and `versionDate` are left out and the hints end with a `file.faulty` warning, as in element.get. An unknown reference is the error ref.unknown, one that fits several elements ref.ambiguous with details.candidates. A short ID whose prefix fits no element stays ref.unknown, never another element; when its tail fits exactly one element of another type, details.candidates names that element and the message asks whether its short ID was meant (prefix may be outdated).

criterion.title: Number
criterion.description: With a reference to an acceptance criterion: that criterion of the current version, with its number, key, text and reference. A key no criterion of the current version carries is ref.unknown with `details.criterion`; a key two criteria carry is ref.ambiguous with the element as the one candidate and their numbers in `details.criteria`. Left out without such a reference.

current.title: Current
current.description: Whether the given version is the element's current version, computed from its file as it is now: "current" or "outdated"; "unknown" when the element has no version to compare with (a value that counts has no normal form, `.inf` or `.nan`, `element` comes without `version` and with a `file.faulty` warning that says why); null when no version was given. Strings, not booleans, so a caller that tests the field for truth never takes "unknown" for current.

names.title: Named elements
names.description: The elements the element names by UUID only, as element.get gives them: the variants of `validity`, `replacedBy` and `excludedBy`, the replacements and the views of `verification`. Left out when it names none.

incomplete.description: A repository of the workspace is not here: replacements, exclusions and records stored there are missing.

outputFields.title: Short ID of the other end

commands.name: element.list
commands.title: List elements
commands.summary: Elements of a selection, sorted; optionally as derivation tree or in groups.

selection.description: Every part given must hold; with `perspective`, in addition to the perspective's selection.

perspective.description: List as the perspective of this name shows it, read from its file on every call, as its saved filter is. Its `where`, its saved filter and every part of `selection` must hold; the view of its saved filter holds, and its `where` is read in the view of `selection`, else its filter's, else the core. `sort` and `group` of the input replace the stored ones. A stored `group` by a text, number or date property whose values can no longer be chosen (more than 30 different values in the workspace, or none that two elements share) gives the list without groups and the warning `perspective.group-unavailable` in `problems`; any other stored key that cannot be grouped is an error. A name no perspective has is input.invalid at `perspective`, one only a faulty file holds file.faulty. A saved filter it names that does not exist is input.invalid at `perspective`, one only a faulty file holds file.faulty, each naming the perspective and the filter; errors of its stored `where`, `sort` and `group` name the perspective and its file.

sort.description: Keys in order; ties go to the next key, then to the workspace order. `hierarchy` only first: the list is then the derivation tree (`tree`). Without sort, the first stored sort of: the saved filter in `selection.filter`, the perspective, the perspective's saved filter, also a stored `sort: []`. An explicit sort, also `[]`, wins over them.

group.description: Group the list: `type` (as written, a subtype is a group of its own), `status`, `package` (the property with the meaning `packages`), or the key of a property whose values element.facets offers: a choice or relation property, or a text, number or date property with few values shared in the workspace (a topic, not a title). Whether a text, number or date key can be grouped follows the data of the workspace (the element.facets rule with its default maxValues of 30), so the same key can become input.invalid as the data changes. Any other key is input.invalid. Groups come in the order a sort by the value gives: types, statuses and choices in metamodel order (a choice written by its display name is in the group of that choice), then other values: numbers, texts ignoring case, booleans; packages and other targets by title ignoring case, then short ID. Elements without a value form the last group; so do elements whose targets are all not available (`unavailable`). Relation items are read as element.facets and the condition `property eq` read them. An element with several values (packages, a list) is in each of their groups. `sort` (or the stored sort) orders the elements inside each group; with `hierarchy` each group is its own tree. Nothing is stored.

items.description: Property values come with `properties`.

fields.description: Give only these fields of each element, in `partial` instead of `elements`; unlike the `fields` of element.search, which says where to search. `id`, `shortId`, `repository` and the `problems` of an element are always given; a field the element has no value for stays left out, as without `fields`. `text` gives the text, also with `withText` false. Without `fields`, every field in `elements`.

withText.description: Also give the text of each element. Left out for an element without a version, and when its file changed while the list was built (list again).

withVerification.description: Also give what each row shows of its element's verification, in `rowVerification`.

limit.description: The most elements on one page.

elements.title: Elements
elements.description: Without `fields`: one page of the list. With `group`, or a perspective that stores one, the page of the grouped list (the elements of the first group, then of the next): an element in several groups is listed once in each, so a page can hold it more than once; key the rows by their position, not by the element.

partial.title: Elements
partial.description: Only with `fields`, instead of `elements`: the same page, each element with the fields asked for.

rowVerification.title: Verification per row
rowVerification.description: Only with `withVerification`: for each row of `elements` (or `partial`), in the same order, the verification status of a requirement and the progress ring of a requirement or need, as a node of trace.graph carries them.

tree.title: Tree
tree.description: Only when `sort`, or the sort that applies without it (of the saved filter or the perspective), starts with `hierarchy`: the place in the derivation tree of each element of `elements` (or `partial`), in the same order. With `group`, or a perspective that stores one, each group is its own tree over its elements: a parent outside the group does not count. The list is the tree depth first: each root, then the elements below it. Each element of the selection appears once: below the parent of the list that reaches it at the shortest depth, the first in sort order among equals; an element without a parent in the list is a root, and so is the first element in sort order of a cycle that no root reaches. Its other parents are in its `relations`.

repository.title: Repository
repository.description: Workspace name of the repository of the element.

depth.title: Depth
depth.description: 0 for a root, 1 for an element below it, and so on.

parent.title: Parent
parent.description: The element it is shown below, a parent of it by a derivation; left out for a root. It may lie on an earlier page.

repository.title: Repository
repository.description: Workspace name of the repository of the parent.

groups.title: Groups
groups.description: Only with `group`, or a perspective that stores one: every group of the whole list in order, also those on other pages; a group without elements is not given. `offset` and `rows` follow from the counts and are given for convenience.

offset.title: Offset
offset.description: Only with `group`, or a perspective that stores one: the row the page starts at (the `offset` of the input), so that a page can be headed by its groups without the input.

rows.title: Rows
rows.description: Only with `group`, or a perspective that stores one: the rows of the grouped list, the sum of the counts of `groups`; `offset` and `limit` page over these rows. At least `total`, more when elements are in several groups.

total.title: Total
total.description: Elements in the selection, each once.

problems.title: Problems
problems.description: With `perspective` (else left out unless the sort warns): `perspective.group-unavailable` (warning, with the perspective file) when its stored grouping can no longer be chosen and the list is given without groups. With a sort by `versionDate`: `sort.incomplete` (warning, per repository) when Git did not give the dates of some elements in time; they are listed last.

outputFields.title: Short ID of the other end
Short ID of the other end

commands.name: element.facets
commands.title: Show facets
commands.summary: Types, statuses and property values of the elements of a selection, with counts, to choose a filter from.

selection.description: Every part given must hold. Without it, every element.

search.description: Only the elements of the selection that element.search finds for `query` in `fields`: the facets of a list of search hits restricted to fields. `fields` as in element.search, refused the same way.

maxValues.description: A property of kind text, number or date gives its values only when it has at most this many distinct values in the whole workspace and at least one of them is shared by two elements; otherwise it is free text, found with element.search. Choice and relation properties always give their values.

types.title: Types
types.description: The types of the selected elements as written in the files, with the number of elements of exactly this type (an element of a subtype is not counted under its parent): types of the metamodel in metamodel order with their name, then other type keys in store order (name = key). Types without a selected element are not listed.

key.title: Key
key.description: Key of the type as written in the files.

name.title: Name
name.description: Display name of the type; the key for a type the metamodel does not define.

count.title: Elements
count.description: Selected elements of exactly this type.

statuses.title: Statuses
statuses.description: The statuses of the selected elements as written in the files, with the number of elements: statuses of the metamodel in metamodel order, then other values in store order. Elements without status are not counted.

key.title: Key
key.description: Key of the status as written in the files.

count.title: Elements
count.description: Selected elements with this status.

properties.title: Properties
properties.description: Every property that a type of a selected element has, in the order of the property definitions of the metamodel. Keys no type has are not listed. The counts and values are those of all selected elements, as the filter conditions read them (any type): an element whose type lacks the property counts by the value its file holds (usually none).

name.title: Name
name.description: Display name of the property.

kind.title: Value kind
kind.description: Value kind of the property.

count.title: Elements with a value
count.description: Selected elements that have some value.

missing.title: Elements without a value
missing.description: Selected elements that have no value (absent, null or []); the elements `{ property, op: "missing" }` selects.

distinct.title: Distinct values
distinct.description: Distinct values the property can be filtered on (for a relation property: distinct available targets). Free text without values counts only up to maxValues + 1, see distinctCapped.

distinctCapped.title: More distinct values
distinctCapped.description: Only for free text: there are more distinct values than maxValues, and `distinct` stopped counting at maxValues + 1.

values.title: Values
values.description: Left out for free text (see maxValues). Choices: in metamodel order, then other values as written. Relation targets: by title ignoring case, then short ID. Others: numbers ascending, then texts ignoring case, then booleans. Each value is what a property condition takes with op eq and selects exactly the elements counted: for a relation target its short ID; a choice stored under a name the condition would map to another key, or one that names several choices, is not given. Targets that are not available are left out (a condition cannot name them).

value.title: Value
value.description: The value, as `{ property, op: "eq", value }` selects it.

count.title: Elements
count.description: Selected elements that have this value.

name.title: Name
name.description: Display name of a choice.

title.title: Title
title.description: Title of a relation target; left out when it has none.

identifier.title: Identifier
identifier.description: Identifier of a relation target, when it has one.

commands.name: element.update
commands.title: Update element
commands.summary: Change title, text or properties of one element. Unknown properties are kept, and unset removes one; status changes only via element.setStatus, and the origin of an imported element only via reqif.import.
commands.whileReadOnlyReason: Changes an element file, and no change can be checked against a missing or faulty metamodel.

text.description: New Markdown text of the element; the blank line after the closing `---` is not part of the text, so the text element.get gives can be passed back unchanged. A changed text gets a final line break. Another element is named by a Markdown link, `[Title](reqseq:N-6010df)` with its UUID, short ID or identifier, which is written as UUID and version; `reqseq:N-6010df` alone is no link and counts for nothing.

setItems.description: List items by position from 1: 1..n replace, n+1.. append; other items keep their bytes, but each acceptance criterion is written with its key.

addRelations.description: Relations to add by kind, as relation.add adds them, in the same write. A relation the element has with a valid version is kept.

removeRelations.description: Relations to remove by kind, as relation.remove removes them (a UUID as given), in the same write. Nothing to remove is an info problem relation.not-found.

repository.description: Which of the elements ref names is meant: its repository's workspace name. ref.ambiguous and ref.unknown (none of them in it) list them in details.candidates.

expectedFileSha256.description: Write precondition: the fileSha256 the change was made on (element.get). Required with title, text or setItems, else input.invalid (precondition-missing); optional for set, unset and relations alone. Other bytes now: file.changed-on-disk, nothing written, even for no change.

dryRun.description: Dry run: checks and output, no write.

names.title: Named elements
names.description: The elements the element names by UUID only, each once in the order first named: the variants of `validity` and the views and missing children of `verification`, as element.get names them. Left out when it names none.

fileSha256.title: File SHA-256
fileSha256.description: Of the file as written, or as read when nothing changed or in a dry run.

files.title: Files
files.description: Written files, relative to the workspace root; empty in a dry run.

dryRun.title: Dry run
dryRun.description: In a dry run: nothing written.

filesToWrite.title: Files to write
filesToWrite.description: Only in a dry run: the file an update would write, relative to the workspace root; empty when nothing would change.

affected.title: Affected elements
affected.description: The number of directly affected elements: the distinct elements other than this one whose files hold a relation or an inline reference to it, the elements at distance 1 of `trace.affected`. Counted only when the save changed what the version is computed from in normal form n1 or n2 (the content), so also when it changed only the stored version of a reference: a link that stores n1 of this element becomes outdated by it; 0 when only the title or properties that do not count to the version changed, or nothing changed. For an element without a version (a value that counts has no normal form) what the version is computed from is compared, so a save of only its title or status also gives 0.

affectedElements.title: Affected elements
affectedElements.description: The elements `affected` counts, in store order; empty when it is 0.

outputFields.title: Short ID of the other end

commands.name: element.setStatus
commands.title: Set status
commands.summary: Set or remove the status of elements on explicit request of the caller. Besides element.supersede the only command that changes a status; no command changes one on its own. A required property without a value blocks no status.
commands.details: Only a status of each element's type is taken (`statuses` of the type in metamodel.get); an element of a type without status gets none. `status: null` removes the status line where the type's status is optional.
commands.whileReadOnlyReason: Sets a status from the statuses of the metamodel, and no change can be checked against a missing or faulty metamodel.

refs.description: The elements whose status is set or removed.

status.description: Key or display name of a status of the metamodel, in any case; the key is written. It must be a status of the element's type. null removes the status line, only from an element whose type has an optional status: no status, or only statuses marked invalid; else input.invalid with reason status-required.

items.description: Written file, relative to the workspace root.

problems.title: Problems
problems.description: For each element, element.missing-required for each required property without a value; then, with a status the metamodel marks invalid, the hints on relations to these elements.

commands.name: element.supersede
commands.title: Supersede element
commands.summary: Supersede an element: set an invalid status of its type and optionally name a successor (relation with meaning succession, written into the successor's file). There is no delete.
commands.whileReadOnlyReason: Sets an invalid status of the metamodel, and no change can be checked against a missing or faulty metamodel.

status.description: Key or display name of a status of the metamodel, in any case; the key is written. It must be a status of the element's type that the metamodel marks invalid.

successor.description: The element that follows the superseded one. Its file gets the relation with meaning succession.

relation.description: Relation kind with meaning succession to write from the successor; needed only when more than one fits the types and the successor does not already have the relation under exactly one of them.

items.description: Written file, relative to the workspace root.

commands.name: element.bulkUpdate
commands.title: Bulk update elements
commands.summary: Set, add to or remove one property for all elements of a selection; without confirm it only previews what changes. Never id, type or status.
commands.details: Without `confirm` only previews: the number of affected elements and the skipped ones, whose type does not have the property. With `confirm` writes only that property's lines. element.setStatus takes several refs for a status. A failed write is rolled back, but a crash can leave part of the selection written: repeat the same call without `expected` and `plan`, which writes only the remaining elements.
commands.whileReadOnlyReason: Changes element files, and no change can be checked against a missing or faulty metamodel.

selection.description: The elements whose property is changed.

property.description: A property of the metamodel; not the title key, not a relation kind.

operation.description: set: replace the value. add: append the items an element does not hold yet (a property with many). remove: without value the property, with value these items (many).

value.description: For set and add. A choice by key or name; relation targets as for element.update.

confirm.description: Write the change; without it nothing is written. A written file also gets the current titles of its same-repository relation targets, which the preview does not show.

expected.description: The count of the preview: with confirm, refused (nothing written) when the change now affects another number of elements. Prefer plan.

plan.description: The preview's plan: with confirm, refused (nothing written) unless the same files get the same bytes.

applied.title: Written
applied.description: True when the files were written (confirm).

count.title: Affected elements
count.description: Number of affected elements.

affected.title: Affected elements
affected.description: The elements whose file the change rewrites, in store order.

unchanged.title: Unchanged elements
unchanged.description: Elements of the selection that have the result already: those of `unchangedElements`.

unchangedElements.title: Unchanged elements
unchangedElements.description: The elements of the selection that have the result already, in store order.

skipped.title: Skipped elements
skipped.description: Elements left out because the metamodel does not allow the property for them.

repository.title: Repository
repository.description: Workspace name of the repository of its file.

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: `not-a-property`: the type of the element does not have the property. `unknown-type`: the metamodel has no type of the element, so it is only read.

message.title: Message
message.description: Why the element was left out, for people.

files.title: Files
files.description: Written files relative to the workspace root; empty in a preview.

problems.title: Problems
problems.description: Hints at the property in the affected elements after the change: missing required value, value kind, more entries than `max-items`, target types. A preview also names what a confirmation refuses: a not writable folder (file.read-only).

plan.title: Plan
plan.description: Fingerprint of the files the change writes and their new bytes; pass it with confirm.

commands.name: element.assignCriterionKeys
commands.title: Assign criterion keys
commands.summary: Give a criterion key to every acceptance criterion without one in the elements of a selection, and name how many elements changed. Versions and existing criterion keys stay as they are.
commands.details: A criterion stored as plain text gets a new key (`element.criterion-key-missing` names them); a criterion with a key keeps it, also one in another form or used twice, which workspace.check reports. Only the lines of the acceptance criteria change, and the current titles of the file's same-repository relation targets. The new keys follow from the file's content, so the same files get the same keys. An element whose type the metamodel does not know is only read and named in `skipped`. A failed write is rolled back; after a crash, the same call writes the remaining elements.
commands.whileReadOnlyReason: Which property holds the acceptance criteria comes from the metamodel, and no change can be checked against a missing or faulty metamodel.

selection.description: The elements whose acceptance criteria get criterion keys.

count.title: Changed elements
count.description: Number of changed elements.

changed.title: Changed elements
changed.description: The changed elements, in store order, each with the number of its acceptance criteria that got a key.

repository.title: Repository
repository.description: Workspace name of the repository of its file.

assigned.title: Criteria with a new key
assigned.description: Acceptance criteria of the element that got a criterion key.

skipped.title: Skipped elements
skipped.description: Elements of the selection with acceptance criteria without key that were left out.

repository.title: Repository
repository.description: Workspace name of the repository of its file.

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: `unknown-type`: the metamodel has no type of the element, so it is only read.

message.title: Message
message.description: Why the element was left out, for people.

files.title: Files
files.description: Written files relative to the workspace root.

commands.name: element.addAttachment
commands.title: Add attachment
commands.summary: Copy an image, from a local file or given as bytes, into the folder named like the element file, next to it, and return the Markdown that embeds it relatively; once the text embeds it, the image counts to the version. Never replaces a file.
commands.whileReadOnlyReason: Adds a file to an element, and no change can be checked against a missing or faulty metamodel.

ref.description: The element the image is copied for. The copy goes into the folder named like its file.

sourcePath.description: The image to copy: a file ending in .avif, .bmp, .gif, .jpeg, .jpg, .png, .svg or .webp (any case). Give it or content, not both.

content.description: The bytes of the image, base64 (RFC 4648, with padding), at most 20 MiB decoded, so a request stays below the 32 MiB limit of the API and MCP: for an image without a file, such as one pasted or dropped in an editor. Needs name; give it or sourcePath, not both.

name.description: The file name of content, for its extension (which must be one of sourcePath's) and the name of the copy, e.g. Screenshot 2026-11-07.png. Only with content.

repository.description: Which of the elements ref names is meant: the workspace name of its repository, as details.candidates of ref.ambiguous give it (for example one copy of a file whose UUID another file shares). Only the elements ref names count; when none of them lies there, the error is ref.unknown with them as details.candidates.

file.description: Which of the elements ref names is meant: its file, relative to its repository, as details.candidates of ref.ambiguous give it. Give repository too when the same path is in several repositories; when several elements are still left, the error is ref.ambiguous with them.

file.title: Image file
file.description: The image file relative to the workspace root, / as separator, e.g. requirements/SR-825b7146fb54/layout.png. Its name is the source name with only ASCII letters, digits, _ and -, and -2, -3, ... when the folder has that name already; a file there with the same bytes is reused.

markdown.title: Markdown
markdown.description: The image as Markdown with a link relative to the element file, e.g. ![layout](SR-825b7146fb54/layout.png), to insert into the text and save with element.update.

commands.name: element.readImage
commands.title: Read image
commands.summary: Return an image file from the repository of an element, named by the destination of a Markdown image relative to the element file, with its bytes, media type and size, so an agent or the web UI can show an image the text embeds.
commands.details: The destination is read as in the element's text: a backslash before ASCII punctuation is removed, a query and a fragment are dropped, and the rest is percent-decoded (an invalid encoding stays as written). It is not a local path: it never leaves the repository of the element. Refused, in this order, with details.reason: a scheme (https:, data:, file:, C:), a leading /, a .. that leads out of the repository, or a nested Git repository or another repository of the workspace inside this one (image-outside-repository, details.cause scheme, absolute, parent or nested); a file that is not there, a folder, a symbolic link on the way or at the file, a path through .git, node_modules or a folder the workspace file ignores, a name spelled other than on disk (also only in case), a name Windows changes or a \ after decoding (image-missing); a file or folder that cannot be read (file.faulty, image-unreadable); a file over 20 MiB (image-too-large, with details.size and details.limit); and a file whose content is no AVIF, BMP, GIF, JPEG, PNG, WebP or SVG image, whatever its extension (not-an-image). An SVG is returned unchanged.

ref.description: The element whose text would embed the image; the destination is relative to the folder of its file.

destination.description: The destination as a Markdown image of the element's text has it, without <...> and without a title, e.g. SR-825b7146fb54/layout.png or ../images/Wind%20map.svg. The element's text need not embed it.

repository.description: Which of the elements ref names is meant: the workspace name of its repository, as details.candidates of ref.ambiguous give it. Only the elements ref names count; when none of them lies there, the error is ref.unknown with them as details.candidates.

file.description: Which of the elements ref names is meant: its file, relative to its repository, as details.candidates of ref.ambiguous give it. Give repository too when the same path is in several repositories; when several elements are still left, the error is ref.ambiguous with them.

content.title: Content
content.description: The bytes of the file, byte for byte, as base64 (RFC 4648, with padding).

mediaType.title: Media type
mediaType.description: The media type by the content of the file, not by its extension.

size.title: Size
size.description: The size of the file in bytes.

commands.name: relation.options
commands.title: Show relation options
commands.summary: Relation kinds the metamodel allows from an element, each with the types its target may have; search a target with element.search and selection.where: { type: targetTypes }.

ref.description: The element that gets the relation (its source).

kind.description: Only this relation kind: none when the type of the element does not allow it.

kinds.title: Relation kinds
kinds.description: In metamodel order: every relation kind whose source-types allow the type of the element (subtypes count) and whose target-types allow some type; none for an element of a type the metamodel does not know. These are the kinds relation.add accepts.

name.title: Name
name.description: Display name of the relation kind.

targetTypes.title: Target types
targetTypes.description: Every type of the metamodel a target may have, subtypes included, in metamodel order; relation.add refuses a target of another known type.

commands.name: relation.add
commands.title: Create relation
commands.summary: Add a relation; stores target UUID and current version, plus the title only within the same repository. A relation over a limit of the kind is saved too, with a relation.too-many hint.
commands.whileReadOnlyReason: Writes the current version of the target, which depends on the metamodel (which properties count).

source.description: The element whose file gets the relation.

kind.description: The relation kind: its key in the metamodel.

target.description: The element the relation points to.

files.title: Files
files.description: Written files, relative to the workspace root.

commands.name: relation.remove
commands.title: Remove relation
commands.summary: Remove a relation from the source file.
commands.whileReadOnlyReason: Changes an element file, and no change can be checked against a missing or faulty metamodel.

source.description: The element whose file holds the relation.

kind.description: The relation kind of the relation to remove: its key in the metamodel.

target.description: The element the relation to remove points to.

repository.description: Only relations into this repository (workspace name); a relation that names none points into the source's repository. Names the one meant when a UUID has relations into several repositories.

items.description: Written file, relative to the workspace root.

commands.name: trace.chain
commands.title: Show trace chain
commands.summary: Chain up to the top parents and down to evidence, with depth, gaps (also a requirement without a parent) and cycles; one page of nodes at a time, total counts all; the validation records of the root.

ref.description: The element the chain starts from.

direction.description: `up` to the parents, `down` to the children and evidence, `both` for both.

view.description: Only the elements of the chain that this view holds: `core` or a variant ID; without it every element.

maxDepth.description: The deepest level in each direction; without it the chain is followed to its ends.

limit.description: Nodes of the page; total counts all. The walk is always complete: depth, gaps, cycles and incomplete are those of the whole chain. Every page walks the whole chain again; to step through a chain, ask with `maxDepth` instead.

offset.description: Nodes skipped before the page, in the order of `nodes` (the root, then the parents level by level, then the children level by level).

repository.description: Which of the elements ref names is meant: the workspace name of its repository, as details.candidates of ref.ambiguous give it (for example one copy of a file whose UUID another file shares). Only the elements ref names count; when none of them lies there, the error is ref.unknown with them as details.candidates.

file.description: Which of the elements ref names is meant: its file, relative to its repository, as details.candidates of ref.ambiguous give it. Give repository too when the same path is in several repositories; when several elements are still left, the error is ref.ambiguous with them.

nodes.title: Nodes
nodes.description: Every element of the chain once per direction, at its shortest depth: the root first, then the parents level by level, then the children level by level. An element reached again (a diamond, a cycle) is not repeated; its edge is in `edges`. In a view, only the elements the view holds (not a core requirement the variant excludes or replaces, nor what hangs only below it); the root always. An element is named by its UUID and `repository`; two files of one repository with the same UUID are two nodes, told apart only by `file`, and edges and gaps name both the same way. Only the page of `limit` nodes from `offset` (in this order) is listed; `total` counts every node. A chain can be large (in a workspace of 50,000 elements and 200,000 relations up to about 42,000 nodes): a client asks for the first page and further ones as needed, or shows it step by step with `maxDepth` 1 and asks again below an element that is not `expanded`.

identifier.title: Identifier
identifier.description: Its identifier (the value of its property with the meaning `identifier`, such as SR-036), for display next to `shortId`; left out when it has none.

type.title: Type
type.description: Key of its type.

status.title: Status
status.description: Its status key as written; left out when it has none.

repository.title: Repository
repository.description: Workspace name of the repository of its file.

file.title: File
file.description: Path relative to the repository.

depth.title: Depth
depth.description: Steps from the root: 0 for the root, 1 for its parents or children, and so on.

direction.title: Direction
direction.description: `up` for a parent (and its parents), `down` for a child (and its children); left out for the root.

expanded.title: Expanded
expanded.description: Its parents or children were looked at; false only at `maxDepth`, where the chain was cut.

total.title: Total
total.description: The number of all nodes of the chain; `nodes` holds the page of `limit` from `offset`.

edges.title: Edges
edges.description: Every derivation relation the chain followed, from the child that stores it (`source`) to its parent (`target`): the upward ones, then the downward ones, in the order they were followed. Paged with the nodes: an edge is listed on the page of the node it leads to in its walk (upwards the parent, downwards the child), so every edge is on exactly one page.

sourceRepository.title: Repository of the source
sourceRepository.description: Workspace name of the repository of `source`.

targetRepository.title: Repository of the target
targetRepository.description: Workspace name of the repository of `target`.

kind.title: Relation kind
kind.description: Key of the relation kind with the meaning `derivation`.

direction.title: Direction
direction.description: The walk it belongs to: `up` to the parents, `down` to the children.

cyclic.title: In a cycle
cyclic.description: Both ends lie in one cycle of derivations.

gaps.title: Gaps
gaps.description: The gaps of the chain, in the order of `nodes` (the `no-parent` gaps of the upward chain first, the root's among them, then those of the downward chain), only those of the nodes of the page. Downward, only for elements whose children were looked at (`expanded`): `no-child` for a need without a child, `no-evidence` for a requirement without a child and without evidence. Upward, only for elements whose parents were looked at, so not with `direction: down`: `no-parent` for a requirement that names no parent through a relation kind with the meaning `derivation`, whatever the view, the status and the availability of the target (a parent in a repository that is not here is one); the metamodel says which kinds derive, so in the standard model a requirement based only on a decision (`based-on`) has the gap. `workspace.check` reports the same elements (`trace.no-parent`). `no-evidence`: the element has no verification record in `view`, in the core without `view` (as `evidence.coverage` and the filter condition `verification`; any version and result). A test case that was only skipped does not close the gap. `not-in-view`: a requirement without a child that `view` does not hold, without `view` the core (its validity names only variants), instead of `no-evidence`, whatever its records; `views` names the views that hold it. It is no evidence gap: a client that counts the gaps of a chain leaves it out. With `view` only the root can have it, as the chain reaches only elements the view holds.

repository.title: Repository
repository.description: Workspace name of the repository of the element with the gap.

kind.title: Gap
kind.description: The kind of the gap, as `gaps` describes it.

views.title: Views
views.description: Only with `not-in-view`: the views that hold the element, `core` first, then the variants in store order; empty when none does (a validity that names no variant of the workspace). `names` names the variants.

evidence.title: Evidence
evidence.description: The evidence of the downward chain, in the order of `nodes`, only for the nodes of the page whose children were looked at (`expanded`), paged like `gaps`; one item per element that has any, none with `direction` `up`. Only verification records; the validation records of the root are in `validationRecords`. With `view` only the records that hold in it (the core the records without a variant, a variant those for it and, for an element of a repository marked `variant-independent`, those without a variant); without `view` every record, each with its `variant`, as `evidence.list`. A test case all of whose executions of the element hold in another view is left out; a test case that was only skipped shows in every view. The evidence document of a record is where its `evidence` points; a JUnit execution has none, its evidence document is its record file (`repository`, `file`, `line`; for automatic tests the record is the result file). These places are text and never opened.

id.title: Element
id.description: The element of the chain the evidence belongs to.

repository.title: Repository
repository.description: Workspace name of the repository of that element.

depth.title: Depth
depth.description: The element's depth plus one: the evidence is one level below it.

testCases.title: Test cases
testCases.description: The test cases that name the element, by class name, then name, each with the element's own executions newest first (`elements` names every element the test case names); `executed` false for a test case that was only skipped.

records.title: Records without test case
records.description: Unlike `evidence.list` `records`: only the element's records without a test case (inspection, analysis, demonstration, manual records without `test-case`), newest first.

validationRecords.title: Validation records
validationRecords.description: The validation records of the root (the validation shown apart from the verification), newest first, those with a test case too, in either direction; on the page with the root only (`offset` 0), `[]` on the others. `view` does not narrow them: a validation record names no variant and holds for its element, as its validation status counts it.

unresolved.title: Unresolved relations
unresolved.description: Derivation relations the chain could not follow: upwards a parent that is not available, downwards a child whose relation points at a UUID several files of the repository share. The other end is shown by its short ID only when it is not available (prefix `UNKNOWN` when its repository is not on this machine). A parent whose `id` is no UUID is not listed (the value-kind check reports it); in a repository that is not here it still makes the chain `incomplete`. Only those of the nodes of the page (`from`).

direction.title: Direction
direction.description: `up` for a parent that could not be followed, `down` for a child.

from.title: From
from.description: The element of the chain whose parents or children were looked at.

fromRepository.title: Repository of the start
fromRepository.description: Workspace name of the repository of `from`.

id.title: Other end
id.description: The other end: the parent the relation names (up), the child that stores it (down).

shortId.title: Short ID of the other end

identifier.title: Identifier of the other end
identifier.description: Identifier of the other end, when it is available and has one.

title.title: Title of the other end
title.description: Title of the other end, when it is available.

targetState.title: Target state
targetState.description: As in `data-export.schema.json#/$defs/relation`; downwards always `ambiguous` (the element the child points at).

incomplete.description: True when a part of the chain lies in a repository that is not on this machine, in the view of a variant while a repository of the workspace is not on this machine (it may hold a replacement or an exclusion), or an evidence location does: evidence and validation records there are not seen.

names.title: Named elements
names.description: The root, then the variants that the records of `evidence` name by UUID only (`variant`), then those the `views` of `gaps` name, each once in the order first named, so a reader names them by short ID, identifier and title on every page. Left out for a variant in a repository that is not here.

problems.title: Problems
problems.description: Hints: `trace.cycle` once per cycle of derivations in the chain, naming its elements; `metamodel.meaning-unassigned` when no type has the meaning `need` or `requirement`, so those gaps cannot be found (upward only `requirement`). The hints are those of the whole chain, on every page.

outputFields.title: Short ID of the other end

commands.name: trace.related
commands.title: Show related elements
commands.summary: All children of a set of parents, or all parents of a set of requirements, each once, optionally up to a depth; one page at a time, total counts all.

refs.description: The elements to start from: the parents for `children`, the requirements for `parents`.

direction.description: `children`: every element derived from them. `parents`: every element they derive from.

maxDepth.description: The most derivation steps from the start elements; without it every step.

view.description: Only the elements that this view holds: `core` or a variant ID; without it every element.

limit.description: Elements of the page; total counts all.

offset.description: Elements skipped before the page, in the order of the list (by distance from the selection).

total.title: Total
total.description: The number of all related elements; `elements` holds the page.

outputFields.title: Short ID of the other end

commands.name: trace.affected
commands.title: Show affected elements
commands.summary: Elements affected by a change of one element, with path and distance.

limit.description: The most elements on one page.

repository.description: Which of the elements ref names is meant: the workspace name of its repository, as details.candidates of ref.ambiguous give it (for example one copy of a file whose UUID another file shares). Only the elements ref names count; when none of them lies there, the error is ref.unknown with them as details.candidates.

file.description: Which of the elements ref names is meant: its file, relative to its repository, as details.candidates of ref.ambiguous give it. Give repository too when the same path is in several repositories; when several elements are still left, the error is ref.ambiguous with them.

affected.title: Affected elements
affected.description: The page of `limit` affected elements from `offset` (`total` counts all). The affected elements: every element that has a relation or an inline reference (in the text or in a property marked `markdown`) to the element, directly or through the chain, each once at its shortest distance, breadth first, the element itself never. Distance 1: every element whose file holds a relation (any relation kind or relation-valued property) or an inline reference to it. From there onward along the derivation chain (meaning `derivation`) and inline references that point at an affected element.

identifier.title: Identifier
identifier.description: Its identifier (the value of its property with the meaning `identifier`, such as SR-036), for display next to `shortId`; left out when it has none.

type.title: Type
type.description: Key of its type.

repository.title: Repository
repository.description: Workspace name of the repository of its file.

file.title: File
file.description: Path relative to the repository.

distance.title: Distance
distance.description: Steps from the element: 1 when this element's file points at it directly.

path.title: Path
path.description: The way: the element asked for first, this element last, each element in between that points at the one before it; each named by UUID and repository.

repository.title: Repository
repository.description: Workspace name of the repository of this element of the path.

via.title: Via
via.description: How this element points at the one before it on the path: a relation stored under `key` (a relation kind or a relation-valued property), or an inline reference in its text or in a property marked `markdown`.

kind.title: Relation or reference
kind.description: `relation`: a relation or relation property stored under `key`. `reference`: an inline reference.

total.title: Total
total.description: The number of all affected elements; `affected` holds the page of `limit` from `offset`.

records.title: Records of older versions
records.description: The evidence records of an older version of the element: its records in the evidence folders whose `version` is not its current one, newest first. Empty when its current version cannot be computed (its file no longer holds it, an embedded image cannot be read).

incomplete.description: True while a repository of the workspace file is not on this machine: elements there may point at the element.

commands.name: trace.neighbourhood
commands.title: Show neighbourhood
commands.summary: The elements reached from one element over its relations and inline references, of every relation kind, up and down to a depth; each edge says whether it repeats an element and whether it is outdated. One page of nodes at a time.

ref.description: The element whose relations and references are walked.

repository.description: The workspace name of the repository of the element ref names, as in element.get.

direction.description: `up`: along the relations and references the element's file stores (its parents, the targets of its other relations and relation properties, its inline references). `down`: along the relations and references that point at it (its children and every element whose file has a relation or an inline reference to it). The source of a relation or reference is placed below its target.

maxDepth.description: The deepest depth in each direction; 0: the root only. Omitted: 1 (the direct neighbours), unless `allLevels` is true.

allLevels.description: Walk as far as the relations and references go (the whole chain); not together with `maxDepth`. For the chain alone ask with `meanings: ["derivation"]`.

kinds.description: Keys of relation kinds or of properties of kind `relation` (such as `packages`) to follow. An unknown key is `input.invalid`. See `meanings` for the filter rule.

meanings.description: Relation kinds with these meanings are followed; `reference` stands for inline references. Without `kinds` and `meanings` every relation and reference is followed. Otherwise a relation or reference is followed when its key is in `kinds` or its meaning is in `meanings`; an empty list follows nothing.

view.description: Only the elements reached that this view holds: `core` or a variant ID; without it every element.

limit.description: Nodes of the page; total counts all.

offset.description: Nodes skipped before the page, in the order of `nodes` (the root, the up walk level by level, the down walk level by level).

nodes.title: Nodes
nodes.description: Every element reached once per walk, at its shortest depth: the root, then the up walk, then the down walk, each level by level. In a view only the elements the view holds (not a core requirement the variant excludes or replaces); the root always. Only the page of `limit` nodes from `offset` is listed; `total` counts all.

identifier.title: Identifier
identifier.description: Its identifier (the value of its property with the meaning `identifier`, such as SR-036), for display next to `shortId`; left out when it has none.

type.title: Type
type.description: Key of its type.

status.title: Status
status.description: Its status key as written; left out when it has none.

repository.title: Repository
repository.description: Workspace name of the repository of its file.

file.title: File
file.description: Path relative to the repository.

depth.title: Depth
depth.description: Steps from the root in its walk: 0 for the root.

direction.title: Direction
direction.description: `up` for an element reached along the relations and references its file stores, `down` for one reached along those that point at it; left out for the root.

expanded.title: Expanded
expanded.description: Its relations and references were looked at; false only at `maxDepth`, where the walk was cut.

total.title: Total
total.description: The number of all nodes; `nodes` holds the page.

edges.title: Edges
edges.description: Every relation and reference the walks followed, up edges first, then down edges, in walk order; an edge is on the page of the node it leads to in its walk. A hub (a package with many members) can put many edges on one page: leave out `packages` with `kinds` or `meanings`. Not listed: unresolved relations and references (`element.get` and `workspace.check` report them).

source.title: Source element
source.description: The element whose file stores the relation or reference.

sourceRepository.title: Repository of the source
sourceRepository.description: Workspace name of the repository of `source`.

target.title: Target element
target.description: The element the relation or reference points at, whatever the walk direction.

targetRepository.title: Repository of the target
targetRepository.description: Workspace name of the repository of `target`.

link.title: Relation or reference
link.description: A relation in the frontmatter or an inline reference in the text or in a property marked `markdown`.

kind.title: Relation kind
kind.description: The frontmatter key, only for `link: relation`.

property.title: Property
property.description: The key is a property of kind `relation` (such as `packages`), not a relation kind.

meaning.title: Meaning
meaning.description: The meaning of the relation kind, `reference` for an inline reference; left out for a kind without a meaning and for a property.

cyclic.title: In a cycle
cyclic.description: Both ends lie in one cycle of the walk.

repeated.title: Repeated
repeated.description: The edge leads, in its walk, to an element that this walk first reached through another edge, or to the root: a repetition. It holds within one call (asking again from a child loses it; to open a tree level by level ask from the same root with a larger `maxDepth`) and within the followed kinds (the tree of derivations comes from `meanings: ["derivation"]`). First means first reached breadth first.

outdated.title: Outdated
outdated.description: The relation or reference stores a version of normal form 1 or 2, its target is available and has a current version, and the two differ, compared in the stored version's form.

incoming.title: Incoming by kind
incoming.description: The relations and references that point at the root directly, as the down walk follows them: one group per property of kind `relation` (such as `packages`), then per relation kind, each in the order of the metamodel, then one for the inline references; only the keys with at least one element. Each element is in a group once, also with several relations of its key, and so is the root where it points at itself. In a view only the elements the view holds, but a successor of the root (a relation kind with the meaning `succession`) in any view. Given when the root's incoming links were looked at: `direction` `down` or `both`, and `maxDepth` not 0. Not paged by `limit` and `offset`.

link.title: Relation or reference
link.description: Relations of one key, or the inline references.

kind.title: Relation kind
kind.description: The frontmatter key, only for `link: relation`.

property.title: Property
property.description: The key is a property of kind `relation` (such as `packages`), not a relation kind.

meaning.title: Meaning
meaning.description: The meaning of the relation kind, `reference` for the inline references; left out for a kind without a meaning and for a property.

count.title: Count
count.description: The number of all elements of the group; `element.list` with this count gives them all.

elements.title: Elements
elements.description: The first 100 elements of the group: by identifier ascending in natural order (digit runs as numbers, case ignored), the elements with the same identifier by short ID, and the elements without an identifier last, by short ID.

identifier.title: Identifier
identifier.description: Its identifier; left out when it has none.

type.title: Type
type.description: Key of its type.

status.title: Status
status.description: Its status key as written; left out when it has none.

repository.title: Repository
repository.description: Workspace name of the repository of its file.

names.title: Named elements
names.description: The root, so a reader names it by short ID, identifier and title on every page, also one whose `nodes` do not hold it.

commands.name: trace.matrix
commands.title: Show traceability matrix
commands.summary: Traceability matrix of a selection: one row per element, one column per relation kind and direction, each cell the elements at the other end, with outdated and missing marks and per column how many rows have a relation.
commands.details: Rows in list order, columns for each kind and direction that occurs. Gaps only where the metamodel sets a minimum (limits with min): such a column also gives how many of the rows it applies to meet it, and their share, and marks the rows below it. One page of rows at a time. With evidence locations also each requirement's test cases and verification status, and the degree.

selection.description: The rows: every element the selection selects, as `element.list` selects them (every part given must hold).
