In a variant view (`selection.view`, or the view of the saved filter) a relation whose other end the view does not hold (also a core requirement the variant excludes or replaces) is left out of the cells and the counts, as `trace.neighbourhood` leaves it out of its walk.

sort.description: As in `element.list`: the rows are in the order `element.list` gives for the same `selection` and `sort`. Without `sort`, the sort of the saved filter in `selection.filter`. `hierarchy` first makes the rows the derivation tree and gives each row its `depth`.

kinds.description: Keys of the relation kinds or of properties of kind `relation` (such as `packages`) to make columns of. An unknown key is `input.invalid`. Without `kinds`, the columns are the relation kinds of the metamodel (Beziehungsarten): relation properties such as the package and the validity are their own built-in meanings and form a column only when named here; inline references are no relation kind and never form a column.

limit.description: Rows of the page; `total` counts all.

offset.description: Rows skipped before the page, in the order of the list.

columns.title: Columns
columns.description: One column per relation kind and direction that occurs in the whole selection, not only on the page: a kind or direction no row has makes no column, except the `out` column of a relation kind whose limits set a minimum (`min` of 1 or more) for the type of a row, which is there even when no row has such a relation. Order: relation kinds in the order of the metamodel, then properties of kind `relation` in property order; per key `out` before `in`. `type` says what a column holds and so the shape of its cells; every column is `relation`. The evidence columns are no column type: their header is `evidence` and their cells are `rows[].testCases` and `rows[].verification`, so a reader of `columns` and `cells` needs no other shape.

type.title: Cell type
type.description: The column holds relations: its cell in each row is an array of relations (`data-export#/$defs/relation`) of `kind` and `direction`. The evidence columns are `evidence`, `rows[].testCases` and `rows[].verification`, not a column type.

kind.title: Relation kind
kind.description: Key of the relation kind, or of the property of kind `relation`.

property.title: Property
property.description: `kind` is the key of a property of kind `relation`, not of a relation kind.

meaning.title: Meaning
meaning.description: The meaning of the relation kind; left out for a kind without a meaning and for a property.

direction.title: Direction
direction.description: `out`: the relations the row element's file stores. `in`: the relations of other elements that point at it.

name.title: Column
name.description: For `out`, the `name` of the kind (e.g. Derives from); for `in`, its `inverse-name` (e.g. Derived by), the `name` when it has none. A name can be the same for both directions (Distinct from): `direction` tells them apart.

count.title: Rows with a relation
count.description: How many rows of the whole selection have at least one relation in this column, whatever the status or availability of its other end; a relation to a missing target counts. With a view, the relations the cells show. 0 only for a column with minima that no row has a relation in.

expected.title: Rows with a minimum
expected.description: Only on the `out` column of a relation kind whose limits set a minimum (`min` of 1 or more) for the type of a row of the whole selection: how many rows have such a minimum. Rows of an unknown type or with a status the metamodel marks invalid have none. Left out on every other column, which has no gap and no share.

met.title: Rows that meet the minimum
met.description: With `expected`, how many of those rows meet all minima of the kind, counted as `hint.list` counts for `relation.too-few`: a relation counts when its target is one element of a known type within the minimum's target type; with a view, only a target that applies in it. A row whose count an unreachable target leaves open is not met and no gap.

share.title: Share
share.description: With `expected`, `met` divided by `expected`. Left out on a column without a minimum.

rows.title: Rows
rows.description: The page: one row per element of the list, in its order.

repository.title: Repository
repository.description: Workspace name of the repository of the element.

identifier.title: Identifier
identifier.description: Its identifier (the value of its property with the meaning `identifier`, such as SR-036), for display next to `shortId`; left out when it has none.

type.title: Type
type.description: Key of its type.

status.title: Status
status.description: Its status key as written; left out when it has none.

file.title: File
file.description: Path relative to the repository.

depth.title: Depth
depth.description: Only when `sort` starts with `hierarchy`: the depth of the element in the derivation tree, as `element.list` gives it in `tree`.

testCases.title: Test cases
testCases.description: Only with `evidence`, on a row whose type has the meaning `requirement` and that applies in its view. The test cases that name the requirement, with their verification executions that hold in the view of `evidence` (`trace.chain` shows the same test cases in the same view), by class name then name; an empty array when it has none: a gap. Records without a test case (inspection, analysis, a manual record without `test-case`) are not here; they count for `verification` only. The chain and `evidence.list` give every execution.

name.title: Test case
name.description: The JUnit `name`, or the `test-case` of the Markdown records.

className.title: Class name
className.description: The JUnit `classname`; left out for a test case of Markdown records.

executed.title: Executed
executed.description: The test case has at least one execution of this requirement in the view.

last.title: Last execution
last.description: The last execution: the newest execution of this requirement in the view, of any version, and of several equally new ones a failed one, with result, date, item and version; its record file (`repository`, `file`, `line`) is the evidence document of a JUnit execution. Left out when `executed` is false.

mark.title: Mark
mark.description: How the cell is marked, the first that holds: `not-executed` when `executed` is false; `outdated` when no execution in the view is of the requirement's current version, or its current version is not known; `failed` when the newest execution of the current version failed, of several equally new ones when one of them failed, as the verification status counts them. Left out otherwise, also when a newer execution of an older version is `last`.

verification.title: Verification status
verification.description: Only with `evidence`, on a row whose type has the meaning `requirement` and that applies in its view. Its verification status in the view of `evidence`, one entry, the same as `element.get` and `evidence.status` give for that view: `indirect` when it is verified through its children.

cells.title: Cells
cells.description: One cell per entry of `columns`, in the same order; a cell takes its shape from the type of its column. For `relation`, an array of the relations of the row element in the column's `kind` and `direction`, each with `shortId` and `title` of the other end when it is available, and an empty array when it has none. An empty cell is no gap by itself: `gaps` names the gaps. Outgoing relations come in the order of the file, incoming ones in the order of the incoming index (store order). A relation to an older version of its target is `outdated`, one to a target that is not there has `targetState: "missing"`; for an incoming relation, `outdated` means its source stores an older version of the row element and `currentVersion` is the row element's.

gaps.title: Gaps
gaps.description: The minima of the row that its cells undershoot, one entry per minimum, in column order and then metamodel order; a cell is a gap when an entry names its column. Only `out` columns of relation kinds whose limits set a minimum for the row's type; a cell can hold relations and be a gap (to a missing target, or to an element of another type). Counted as `expected` and `met` count. Left out when the row has none.

column.title: Column
column.description: The index of the column in `columns`, and so of the cell in `cells`.

targetType.title: Target type
targetType.description: The target type of the minimum.

count.title: Relations
count.description: The relations that count for the minimum, as `relation.too-few` gives `count`.

min.title: Minimum
min.description: The minimum, the `min` of the limit (the `limit` of `relation.too-few`; not the page size `limit` of the input).

total.title: Total
total.description: The number of rows of the whole selection.

incomplete.description: The selection is incomplete, or the workspace file lists a repository that is not on this machine: relations of elements there that point at a row cannot be seen, and its elements may belong to the selection. With `evidence`, also when an evidence location lies in such a repository: its records are not seen.

evidence.title: Evidence header
evidence.description: The header of the evidence columns: given when the workspace file names an evidence location, the metamodel is valid and the selection holds an element whose type has the meaning `requirement`; then every requirement row of the page that applies in `view` has `testCases` and `verification`. Other rows have neither (a requirement that applies only in variants, without a view): not applicable, no gap. Left out otherwise, and the output is the one without evidence.

view.title: View
view.description: The one view of the test cases, the status and the degree: the selection's view, else its saved filter's, else the core (as `evidence.degree`). `element.get` and `evidence.status` give every view.

degree.title: Verification degree
degree.description: The verification degree of the whole selection in `view`, with the count per status, not of the page only; the same as `evidence.degree` gives for the same selection.

names.title: Named elements
names.description: The elements that `evidence` and the rows' `verification` name by UUID only, each once in the order first named: the variant of the view and the missing children (`missingChildren`), so a reader names them by short ID, identifier and title. Left out when they name none.

outputFields.title: Short ID of the other end

commands.name: trace.graph
commands.title: Show graph
commands.summary: The graph of one element: what its relations and references lead to above it and what points at it below, to a depth, over the chosen kinds, with each requirement's verification status.
commands.details: Each element is one node with its level and marks, each requirement with its verification status and each need with the verification degree of its derived requirements, and each relation or reference between two nodes is one edge. At most `limit` nodes, nearest levels first. With `withEvidence` also a summary of the evidence below each element.

ref.description: The element whose graph is shown.

repository.description: The workspace name of the repository of the element ref names, as in element.get.

maxDepth.description: The deepest level in each direction; 0: the element only. Omitted: 1 (the direct neighbours), unless `allLevels` is true.

allLevels.description: Go as far as the relations and references go (the whole chain), within `limit`; not together with `maxDepth`. For the chain alone ask with `meanings: ["derivation"]`.

kinds.description: Keys of relation kinds or of properties of kind `relation` (such as `packages`) to follow. An unknown key is `input.invalid`. See `meanings` for the filter rule.

meanings.description: Relation kinds with these meanings are followed; `reference` stands for inline references. Without `kinds` and `meanings` every relation and reference is followed. Otherwise a relation or reference is followed when its key is in `kinds` or its meaning is in `meanings`; an empty list follows nothing.

view.description: Only the elements of the graph that this view holds, and the verification status in it: `core` or a variant ID; without it every element, and the verification status of the core.

withEvidence.description: Also give `evidence`, a summary of the evidence (verification records and test cases) of each element shown below the element. Evidence is no relation or reference between elements, so `kinds` and `meanings` do not choose it, and it is no node: `limit` counts the elements only.

limit.description: The most nodes, the element included; the nearest levels first (`truncated` says when more exist).

nodes.title: Nodes
nodes.description: Every element of the graph once: the element first, then level by level from the nearest (for each distance the elements above, then those below, each in the order the relations and references were followed). An element reached both ways is one node at its smaller distance, above on a tie. In a view only the elements the view holds (not a core requirement the variant excludes or replaces); the element always. At most `limit` nodes.

identifier.title: Identifier
identifier.description: Its identifier (the value of its property with the meaning `identifier`, such as SR-036), for display next to `shortId`; left out when it has none.

type.title: Type
type.description: Key of its type.

status.title: Status
status.description: Its status key as written; left out when it has none.

repository.title: Repository
repository.description: Workspace name of the repository of its file.

file.title: File
file.description: Path relative to the repository.

expanded.title: Expanded
expanded.description: Its relations and references in the direction of its level (both for the element) were looked at and every element they lead to is a node. False at `maxDepth`, where `limit` stopped the walk, and when `limit` left out an element they lead to.

level.title: Level
level.description: 0 for the element; -d for an element reached d steps up along the relations and references the files store (its parents, the targets of its other relations and relation properties, its inline references), +d for one reached d steps down along those that point at it. The source of a relation or reference is placed below its target.

marks.title: Marks
marks.description: In this order, only those that hold: `outdated`, the element stores an outdated relation, relation property or inline reference (the `relation.outdated` and `variant.core-changed` hints of element.get), whatever kinds are followed; `superseded`, its status is one the metamodel marks invalid. Empty when none holds. The verification status is `verification`.

verification.title: Verification status
verification.description: The verification status of a requirement (type with the meaning `requirement`) in the graph's view (`view`, the core without one), as element.get gives it for that view: one entry. Left out for any other node, and for a requirement that has no status in that view (it applies only in a variant).

criteria.title: Criteria
criteria.description: How many of the requirement's acceptance criteria are verified, for its progress ring: the entry's `criteria` when its own records in the view decide; without such a record and with acceptance criteria, none verified (0 of n); left out when the status is `indirect`, the requirement has no acceptance criteria, or it has no `verification`.

degree.title: Verification degree
degree.description: For a need (type with the meaning `need`), the verification degree of the requirements derived directly from it, in the graph's view: its derivation children in the whole workspace whatever depth, kinds and meanings the graph shows, each once, counted as evidence.degree counts them. `share` is left out when none counts (no valid derived requirement). Without a relation kind with the meaning `derivation`, or while the metamodel is not valid, none counts.

edges.title: Edges
edges.description: Every followed relation or reference from one node to another, also one the walks did not take (one between two parents, or from a child to a parent): by source in the order of `nodes`, then in the order its file stores them (relations and relation properties in frontmatter order, then inline references). One from an element to itself is no edge. Not listed: unresolved relations and references (`element.get` and `workspace.check` report them).

source.title: Source element
source.description: The element whose file stores the relation or reference.

sourceRepository.title: Repository of the source
sourceRepository.description: Workspace name of the repository of `source`.

target.title: Target element
target.description: The element the relation or reference points at.

targetRepository.title: Repository of the target
targetRepository.description: Workspace name of the repository of `target`.

link.title: Relation or reference
link.description: A relation in the frontmatter or an inline reference in the text or in a property marked `markdown`.

kind.title: Relation kind
kind.description: The frontmatter key, only for `link: relation`.

property.title: Property
property.description: The key is a property of kind `relation` (such as `packages`), not a relation kind.

meaning.title: Meaning
meaning.description: The meaning of the relation kind, `reference` for an inline reference; left out for a kind without a meaning and for a property.

outdated.title: Outdated
outdated.description: The relation or reference stores a version of normal form 1 or 2, its target has a current version, and the two differ, compared in the stored version's form.

evidence.title: Evidence per node
evidence.description: Only with `withEvidence`: one summary of the evidence below each node that has any, in the order of `nodes`; `[]` when none has. Only nodes at level 0 or below whose evidence level (`level`) is within the depth asked (`maxDepth`, every level with `allLevels`), whether `expanded` or not; none above the element. The counts are those of trace.chain's `evidence` (`chainEvidenceOf`) in the view, the core without one: only verification records. The details are in trace.chain and evidence.list.

id.title: Node
id.description: The node the evidence belongs to.

repository.title: Repository
repository.description: Workspace name of the repository of that node.

level.title: Level
level.description: The node's level plus one: the evidence is one level below it.

testCases.title: Test cases
testCases.description: The test cases that name the node and hold in the view, a test case that was only skipped included.

records.title: Records without test case
records.description: The node's verification records without a test case that hold in the view (inspection, analysis, demonstration, manual records without `test-case`).

results.title: Results
results.description: The newest result of each test case (`skipped` for one that was only skipped) and of each record, counted; a result none has is left out.

passed.title: Passed
passed.description: Test cases and records whose newest result passed.

failed.title: Failed
failed.description: Test cases and records whose newest result failed.

inconclusive.title: Inconclusive
inconclusive.description: Test cases and records whose newest result is inconclusive.

skipped.title: Skipped
skipped.description: Test cases that were only skipped.

truncated.title: Truncated
truncated.description: More elements are reachable than shown: `limit` stopped a walk or left out a node. The nodes kept are the nearest ones.

problems.title: Problems
problems.description: Hints: `metamodel.meaning-unassigned` when no relation kind has the meaning `derivation` or no type the meaning `requirement`, so the verification status and degree of the nodes cannot be given in full.

commands.name: trace.mermaid
commands.title: Show graph as Mermaid
commands.summary: The graph of one element as trace.graph gives it, written as a Mermaid flowchart: one node per element, one edge per relation or reference, without the evidence.
commands.details: The same nodes and edges as `trace.graph` for the same input, as text. Each node shows the short ID with the identifier, the type, the title, the marks and the verification; each edge goes from the source to the target and is labelled with the name of its kind, and `outdated` when the relation or reference is outdated. The element has a thicker frame. The first line is a comment when the graph is cut by `limit` or incomplete. The CLI prints the text alone, so its output redirected to a file is a Mermaid diagram. A graph near the default `limit` of 500 nodes can be larger than Mermaid draws with its default settings (at most 500 edges and 50,000 characters of text); for a large graph ask with a smaller `maxDepth` or `limit`.

ref.description: The element whose graph is written.

repository.description: The workspace name of the repository of the element ref names, as in element.get.

maxDepth.description: The deepest level in each direction; 0: the element only. Omitted: 1 (the direct neighbours), unless `allLevels` is true.

allLevels.description: Go as far as the relations and references go (the whole chain), within `limit`; not together with `maxDepth`. For the chain alone ask with `meanings: ["derivation"]`.

kinds.description: Keys of relation kinds or of properties of kind `relation` (such as `packages`) to follow. An unknown key is `input.invalid`. See `meanings` for the filter rule.

meanings.description: Relation kinds with these meanings are followed; `reference` stands for inline references. Without `kinds` and `meanings` every relation and reference is followed. Otherwise a relation or reference is followed when its key is in `kinds` or its meaning is in `meanings`; an empty list follows nothing.

view.description: Only the elements of the graph that this view holds: `core` or a variant ID; without it every element.

limit.description: The most nodes, the element included; the nearest levels first (`truncated` says when more exist).

mermaid.title: Mermaid
mermaid.description: The Mermaid flowchart, bottom to top, LF line endings and a final newline. Labels are quoted, with `#`, `&`, `<`, `>`, `"`, `:` and `{` written as Mermaid entities in node labels and `&`, `<` and `>` in edge labels. In an edge label `"` becomes `'` and `%%{` becomes `%% {`; line breaks and other control characters become one space.

truncated.title: Truncated
truncated.description: More elements are reachable than shown: `limit` stopped a walk or left out a node. The nodes kept are the nearest ones.

problems.title: Problems
problems.description: Hints: `metamodel.meaning-unassigned` when no relation kind has the meaning `derivation` or no type the meaning `requirement`, so the verification status and degree of the nodes cannot be given in full.

commands.name: hint.list
commands.title: List hints
commands.summary: Open hints of the workspace, filterable by kind, type, package or variant; one page of hints at a time, total and the count per kind count all.

kind.description: Only hints with one of these codes.

type.description: Only hints about elements of one of these types, or of a type that extends one of them.

package.description: Only hints about elements whose property with the meaning packages lists this package.

variant.description: Only hints about elements in the view of this variant; a hint about a variant element only for that variant.

ref.description: Only the hints about this element.

limit.description: Hints of the page; total and kinds count all. Every page finds every hint again; only the dates of outdated relations are asked for the hints of the page alone.

offset.description: Hints skipped before the page, in the order of `hints`.

kinds.title: Hints per kind
kinds.description: The number of hints that pass the filters per kind, counted over every such hint, not only the page of `limit` from `offset`. Without `kind`: each kind that has a hint, in the order its first hint has in `hints` over all pages. With `kind`: also each kind it names that has none, with count 0, after the others in the order `kind` names them. The counts add up to `total`.

count.title: Hints
count.description: Hints of this kind that pass the filters.

hints.title: Hints
hints.description: The open hints: problems of severity warning about one element (the element should be checked; a hint blocks nothing and changes no status), from the same whole-workspace problems as workspace.check, after the warning of each element whose version cannot be computed (file.faulty, as element.get gives it), which workspace.check does not give; errors, info and warnings about no element are not hints. Filters combine with AND. Each hint with its kind (code), the element it is about (elementId, repository, file, line, and its title elementTitle), its target where it has one (targetId; with targetRepository, targetShortId, targetIdentifier and targetTitle when it was resolved to one element), for an outdated verification or validation status (`evidence.outdated`) the view whose status is outdated (view) and its reason (message; for an outdated relation with both versions and their dates). In this order: the warnings without a version, then the order of workspace.check. Only the page of `limit` hints from `offset` (in this order) is listed; `total` counts every hint that passes the filters.

total.title: Total
total.description: The number of all hints that pass the filters; `hints` holds the page of `limit` from `offset`.

incomplete.description: True while a repository of the workspace file is not on this machine: the hints of its elements are not listed.

commands.name: hint.confirm
commands.title: Confirm hints
commands.summary: Confirm hints after a person reviewed them: by hint ID, all confirmable hints of one element, or those of the whole workspace with some codes. It writes the current version of the target into the relation, the inline reference or the `replaces` item.
commands.details: With all, `expected` is the total of hint.list with that kind. It writes the current target version into the relation or inline reference (in the text or in a property marked `markdown`; `relation.outdated`) or into the `replaces` item (`variant.core-changed`), and nothing else but the current titles of the file's same-repository targets. An ID no open hint has gives a warning, for example one confirmed already.
commands.whileReadOnlyReason: Writes the current version of the target, which depends on the metamodel (which properties count).

input.description: Give `hintIds`, `ref`, `target`, `all` or several of them; none is `input.invalid`. `ref` and `target` select the open confirmable hints (with a `hintId`, as hint.list gives them) about `ref` and pointing at `target`, both when both are given; `all` selects those of the whole workspace and goes with neither. `kind` narrows only that selection and needs `ref`, `target` or `all`; `all` needs `kind` and `expected`, so a call names the codes and the number of hints a person reviewed and never confirms all by accident. The selected hints and `hintIds` are confirmed together, as one set: each once, `confirmed` names `hintIds` first, then the selected IDs. A selection without an open confirmable hint is a `hint.not-found` warning, left out when the call already gives `hint.not-confirmable` for the since-baseline hints.

hintIds.description: IDs of hints to confirm (`hintId` of hint.list).

ref.description: Confirm the open confirmable hints about this element: the outdated relations and inline references (in the text and in properties marked `markdown`) its file stores, and its `replaces` items onto a changed core requirement. A variant with open `variant.core-changed-since-baseline` or `variant.core-new-since-baseline` hints, without `kind`, gives `hint.not-confirmable` for them, since a new baseline of the variant settles them.

target.description: Confirm the open confirmable hints on relations and inline references that point at this element.

all.description: Select the open confirmable hints of the whole workspace with one of the codes of `kind`: those hint.list gives with a hintId for that `kind` and no other filter. Needs `kind` with confirmable codes only (see `kind`; a since-baseline code is refused with its reason, other codes are `input.invalid`) and `expected`; not with `ref` or `target`.

kind.description: Only selected hints with one of these codes (with `ref`, `target` or `all`); the confirmable codes are `relation.outdated` and `variant.core-changed`; a since-baseline code gives `hint.not-confirmable` (see `ref`).

expected.description: The number of hints the call confirms as the person reviewed them: the hints the selection holds, counted as hint.list counts them (a relation written twice is two hints with one ID), plus one per given hint ID that the selection does not hold (with `all`: `total` of hint.list with the same `kind` and no other filter). When the call would confirm another number, it is refused and nothing is written (`input.invalid`, details `count`), for example after a pull brought new hints. Required with `all`.

confirmed.title: Confirmed hints
confirmed.description: The IDs of the confirmed hints, each once.

files.title: Files
files.description: Written files, relative to the workspace root.

commands.name: element.search
commands.title: Search elements
commands.summary: Full-text search of the elements of a selection in all or chosen fields (title, text, IDs, all properties or single properties), typo tolerant, in any case, with phrases in quotes, the best first, each hit with where it was found and a snippet around the match; optionally in groups.

query.description: Words split at spaces; every word must match in a searched field (the title, the text, a property value, the type or status name, or an ID; with `fields` only those). A word matches words it begins (from 2 letters), words it stands inside after their start (from 4 letters, none for a query word with a digit, without a typo), and with a typo (1 edit from 4 letters, 2 from 8; none for a query word with a digit), in any case; a word found inside a longer word counts less than a whole word or a word start. A short ID, an identifier or at least 6 hex digits of a UUID match that element exactly; ID matches come first. A criterion key, also after `AK-`, also matches each criterion with it, exactly, where the acceptance criteria are searched. A criterion reference of a test name, with or without brackets, matches each requirement its identifier or short ID names with exactly one criterion with the key, as an ID match (with `id`) and in that criterion; its words still match as an ID's, but not in these requirements; one that fits none is plain words. Consecutive words outside quotes that are a designation of an element (its title, a synonym or its translation, when the metamodel gives properties these meanings) also match where one of its other designations stands, from every element that has it: as whole words in this order, without a typo, in any case, the last word also as a word start, in a searched field; the longest designation at each place from the left counts, and the other words must still match. Designations of an element whose status is invalid do not count. After the ID matches come the hits found by every word itself (a word found inside a longer word counts as found itself), then those found through another designation, then those with a word found only in their type or status name, and in no other searched field. Words in quotes (`"`, `„`, `“` or `”`, opening at the start or after a space) are a phrase: they match only one after the other in this order, as whole words, in any case and without a typo, within the title, the text or one value of a property, and not across a paragraph, list item or table cell; characters other than letters and digits between them and a line break within a paragraph do not count. Without a closing quote the phrase runs to the end and its last word also matches the words it begins. Quotes without a word count for nothing; a quoted short ID, identifier, UUID, criterion key or criterion reference still matches as without quotes. In a shell: `reqseq element search '"Filter list"'`. A query without a word finds nothing.

selection.description: Search only within it: a view, a filter, a package or IDs.

fields.description: Search only in these fields; default all. `title`, `text` (the Markdown text), `id` (UUID, short ID, identifier, and a criterion reference), `properties` (all properties, with the type and status names and keys the metamodel does not know; no relations), or the key of a property that holds no relations and is not the title (a choice is found by the names of its values, the acceptance criteria property also by the criterion keys of its criteria); element.searchFields lists them. Every word must be found in a chosen field, itself (also as a word start or inside a longer word) or through another designation, and only they rank a hit; an ID match comes first only with `id`. A word that can match nothing there finds nothing. `properties` with a single property is `properties`. A key that holds relations, the title's key, `type`, `status` or a key the metamodel does not know is `input.invalid`, naming the key. The names `title`, `text`, `properties` and `id` always mean these fields.

group.description: Group the hits by the keys and rules of element.list `group`: the same groups in the same order, a hit with several values in each of their groups, the hits without a value (or with only targets not available) in the last group, and an invalid key `input.invalid` whatever the query finds. Inside each group the hits keep the order of the search (ID matches, then hits found by every word itself, then hits found through another designation, then hits with a word found only in the type or status name, each by relevance, then workspace order). The grouping reads the records the hits were found in; their targets are looked up in the workspace the selection was read from. Nothing is stored.

withVerification.description: Also give what each row shows of its element's verification, in `rowVerification`.

limit.description: The most hits on one page.

output.description: One page of the hits, the best first: ID matches, then hits found by every word itself, then hits found through another designation, then hits with a word found only in the type or status name, each by relevance, then workspace order. Waits for the search index while it is built. The hits of the page read their files for the snippet.

hits.title: Hits
hits.description: One page of the hits. With `group`, the page of the grouped rows (the hits of the first group, then of the next): a hit in several groups is a row in each, so a page can hold it more than once; key the rows by their position, not by the element.

repository.title: Repository
repository.description: Workspace name of the repository of the element.

identifier.title: Identifier
identifier.description: The value of the property with the meaning identifier, when the element has one.

status.title: Status
status.description: The status key as written in the file.

score.title: Score
score.description: Relevance of the matched words, rounded to 6 significant digits; a criterion key found in a criterion adds that of one word found once, in as many elements as carry the key; a word found inside a longer word (also one that is a typo of it) counts less than a whole word or a word start; 0 for an ID match only; through another designation, the relevance of the words and designations found. A hit found through another designation comes after the hits found by every word itself, and a hit with a word found only in its type or status name after both, whatever its score.

fields.title: Fields
fields.description: What a word of the query was found in, among the fields searched, for a phrase or another designation of several words only where it stands whole; a single property is `properties`, and so is a criterion key or reference found in a criterion.

terms.title: Matched words
terms.description: The words of the element that matched the words of the query outside quotes, a phrase of one word or another designation of one word, in lower case, the whole word also when a query word was found only at its start or inside it (the marks give that part); none for an ID, a criterion key found in a criterion, a criterion reference in the requirements it fits, a phrase or another designation of two or more words.

titleMarks.title: Matches in the title
titleMarks.description: The matched words in `title`, of a word found by a word of the query outside quotes only at its start or inside it only that part, the whole word where its letters do not map one by one onto the indexed word, a phrase or another designation of several words as a whole; only when a word, phrase or designation was found in the title.

snippet.title: Snippet
snippet.description: Where a word was found and one line around the first match in reading order, or the start of an acceptance criterion's text where only its key was found, only in the fields searched: in the text when it is searched and a visible word of it matched, else in the first value with a match of a searched property, the properties of the type in metamodel order, then the others in file order. `text` is at most 120 code points, `…` at a cut end included: the visible text without Markdown characters, white space as single spaces; `marks` are the matched words in it, of a word found by a word of the query outside quotes only at its start or inside it only that part, the whole word where its letters do not map one by one onto the indexed word, a phrase or another designation of several words as a whole and none of its words elsewhere. A list item or a nested value is a value of its own; a choice shows its name; an acceptance criterion is named in `criterion`. None when no visible word and no criterion key matched: a match only in the title, an ID, the identifier, the type or status name, a link destination, HTML or an entity, or a file changed since the index read it.

propertyName.title: Property name
propertyName.description: Its name in the metamodel; the key for a property the metamodel does not define.

criterion.title: Criterion
criterion.description: When the value is an acceptance criterion: its number and criterion key, as element.resolve gives them in `criterion`; the snippet stands for its text.

criterion.title: Number
criterion.description: Its position in the current version, from 1.

key.title: Criterion key
key.description: The criterion key; left out without one.

keyMarked.title: Key marked
keyMarked.description: Only its key was found in it: the location highlights the key, and the snippet is the start of its text without marks.

groups.title: Groups
groups.description: Only with `group`: every group of all the hits in order, also those on other pages; a group without hits is not given. `offset` and `rows` follow from the counts.

offset.title: Offset
offset.description: Only with `group`: the row the page starts at (the `offset` of the input).

rows.title: Rows
rows.description: Only with `group`: the rows of the grouped hits, the sum of the counts of `groups`; `offset` and `limit` page over these rows. At least `total`, more when hits are in several groups.

rowVerification.title: Verification per row
rowVerification.description: Only with `withVerification`: for each row of `hits`, in the same order, the verification status of a requirement and the progress ring of a requirement or need, as a node of trace.graph carries them.

commands.name: element.searchFields
commands.title: List search fields
commands.summary: The fields a search can be restricted to, each with its key and name, for choosing the fields of element.search.
commands.details: Title, text, IDs and all properties first, then each property of the metamodel that a type of the workspace's elements has, in metamodel order: one that holds no relations and is not the title. A property whose key is `title`, `text`, `id` or `properties` is not listed, since that key names the fixed field. Every listed key is a value element.search `fields` takes.

fields.title: Fields
fields.description: The fields in the order above.

key.title: Key
key.description: What element.search `fields` takes: `title`, `text`, `id`, `properties` or the key of a property.

name.title: Name
name.description: The name: of the title property for `title` ("Title" without one), "Text", "IDs", "All properties", else the property's name in the metamodel.

commands.name: filter.list
commands.title: List saved filters
commands.summary: Saved filters of the workspace, with their definitions.

filters.title: Saved filters

file.title: File

commands.name: evidence.record
commands.title: Record evidence
commands.summary: Write a manual verification or validation record into an evidence folder of the workspace, for a check that is not an automated test; the element's UUID and current version are filled in.
commands.details: The record is Markdown (evidence-record.schema.json). A verification names a requirement and optionally the acceptance criteria it proves, a validation a need or a requirement. Never replaces a file: a name that is taken gets -2, -3, ...
commands.whileReadOnlyReason: Fills in the current version of the element, which depends on the metamodel (which properties count).

ref.description: The element the record is about. Its UUID and current version are written into the record; neither is an input.

kind.description: Verification of a requirement, or validation of a need or a requirement. Any other element is `input.invalid` with `details.reason` `wrong-type`. A validation record counts for the validation status only.

result.description: The result of the check. `inconclusive` is allowed for a validation only and needs a `reason`.

reason.description: Why the validation is inconclusive: required with the result `inconclusive`, not allowed with any other result. At least one character that is not white space, no control characters other than tab, line feed and carriage return.

item.description: The item under test, for example the build or sample. Required for verification. No white space at either end and no control characters other than tab, line feed and carriage return.

variant.description: A variant the element applies in (an element whose type has the meaning variant); the record holds for it. Absent: the core, and also every variant the element applies in when the element's repository is marked `variant-independent` in the workspace file. Verification only: a variant with `kind` validation is `input.invalid` with `details.reason` `validation-with-variant`. `core` names no variant and is `input.invalid` with `details.reason` `core-is-no-variant`; leave `variant` out for the core. A variant the element is not in is `input.invalid` with `details.reason` `not-valid-in-variant`, or `excluded-in-variant` or `replaced-in-variant` when the variant excludes or replaces the requirement. Absent for a verification of an element the core does not hold, which would then count in no view, is `input.invalid` with `details.reason` `counts-in-no-view`, unless the element's repository is marked `variant-independent` and a variant holds it.

date.description: When the check was done. Default: the time of the call, UTC, whole seconds. Its first ten characters (the day in its own offset) start the file name.

evidence.description: Where the evidence document is: a path relative to the record file, a file URL or any URI. Written as given; ReqSeq never opens it.

testCase.description: Optional test case name or ID (`test-case` in the file).

items.description: An acceptance criterion by its number, counted from 1 (for example 2, not AK2), or by its criterion key (for example k7f3).

anyOf.description: A criterion key, or a number written as digits (the command line passes text).

criteria.description: The acceptance criteria the record holds for, each by its number (the position in the property with the meaning `acceptance-criteria` of the element's current version, counted from 1) or by its criterion key. The file gets their criterion keys, sorted by key. Absent: the record holds for every criterion. `input.invalid`, and nothing is written, for a criterion without key (`details.reason` `criterion-without-key`), a key that several criteria carry (`criterion-key-duplicate`), and a number or key the current version does not have (`unknown-criterion`). Verification only: with `kind` validation it is `input.invalid` with `details.reason` `validation-with-criteria`, because a validation counts per element.

folder.description: The folder to write into: an evidence location of the workspace file or a folder below one, relative to the workspace root (the folder of the main repository) with `/`, for example `evidence/manual` or `../tests/evidence`. Missing folders below the location are created. Default: the first evidence location whose repository is on this machine.

items.description: The written record file, relative to the workspace root as `workspacePath` gives it (with `/`).

criteria.description: With `criteria`: each criterion the record holds for, in the order of the criteria, with its number, its criterion key and the first 60 characters of its text.

criterion.title: Number

text.title: Criterion text

commands.name: evidence.enrichJunit
commands.title: Enrich JUnit file
commands.summary: Tie the test cases of a JUnit XML file to the elements they name, so that the file becomes test evidence. Test cases with an unknown reference or a view that does not fit are listed, and the command fails.
commands.details: A test case names an element by short ID, UUID or identifier, or by a short ID in another form that a name pattern finds; each given view (a variant's UUID, or `core`) is added. Test cases with an unknown reference, or whose views do not fit, stay unchanged and are listed. The output counts the test cases that name no element, and with `skipNotInView` the elements left out because they apply in none of the given views; a test case whose elements all apply in none of them is marked with those views instead of enriched.
commands.whileReadOnlyReason: Writes the current versions of the elements, which depend on the metamodel (which properties count).

file.description: The JUnit XML file to enrich: each test case it enriches gets the element's UUID and version, the item under test, the date and the views run. It is rewritten in place unless `output` is given. A test case that already has a `reqseq:version` is never changed (version from the tested state).

item.description: The item under test, for example the build. No white space at either end and no control characters other than tab, line feed and carriage return.

date.description: The date of the test run. Default: an existing `reqseq:date` of the test case, else the `timestamp` of its test suite when that has a time zone, else the time of the call.

variant.description: The views the test run was for, one or more: a variant by UUID, short ID or identifier, or `core`. Each enriched test case gets a `reqseq:variant` per view, the variant's UUID or `core`; the core alone writes none. Absent: a test case keeps its own `reqseq:variant` properties, if any, whose short ID or identifier becomes the UUID. A test case that names a view not given, or names an element that does not count in one of its views (not valid there, excluded or replaced, as at `evidence.record`), stays unchanged and gets `evidence.invalid-record`; so does an enriched test case (never changed, version from the tested state) with a view not given. The core is checked like a variant when it is given or named; a record without variant counts in the core, and in every view the element applies in when its repository is marked `variant-independent`.

skipNotInView.description: Only with `variant` (else `input.invalid` with `details.reason` `skip-without-views`): an element that applies in none of the given views is left out of the test case instead of refusing it: it gets no `reqseq:element`, `reqseq:version` or `reqseq:criterion`, and `notInView` counts these. A test case with no element left gets no requirement but one `reqseq:not-in-view` property per given view, the variant's UUID or `core`, in the order given; its name and other properties stay. A run with the same views leaves such a mark as it is, one with other views rewrites it, and a run that enriches the test case removes it. The JUnit reader passes over a marked test case without `evidence.not-enriched`. An element that applies in some of them is enriched, and its records count only where it applies. Default false: such a test case stays unchanged and is reported.

namePattern.description: A template that finds a short ID written in another form in test case names, for names that cannot hold brackets, e.g. `{prefix}_{id}_ak_{ak}` for `sr_348143_ak_k7f3` (SR-348143, its criterion `k7f3`). `{prefix}` is a type prefix of the metamodel, `{id}` 6 to 32 hex digits, `{ak}` the criterion key of an acceptance criterion, written as `reqseq:criterion`; a number there, or a key that no criterion or more than one carries in the current version, leaves the test case unchanged with `evidence.invalid-criterion-name`. `{prefix}` and `{id}` once each, `{ak}` once at most and not next to `{id}`. The rest is literal text; `{{` and `}}` are braces, square brackets are refused. All of it is ASCII case-insensitive. A match starts and ends at a word boundary (the start or end of the name, a character that is not a letter or digit, or the start of a camel case word) and is looked for in the name outside `[...]` only, not in the class name. It adds to the bracket form and the `reqseq:element` property; a short ID it finds that names no element, or several, is listed in `unknown`.

output.description: Default: overwrite the input file. An existing file is replaced only when it is a JUnit XML file the scanner accepts; its folder must exist.

testCases.title: Enriched test cases
testCases.description: The test cases that name at least one element and are enriched: by this call, or already before.

withoutReference.title: Test cases without element
withoutReference.description: The test cases that name no element: no `reqseq:element` property and no name token or pattern match that names one (a pytest parameter list counts here). Test cases enriched already, listed in `unknown` or refused are not counted. Information only: it does not change the exit code.

notInView.title: Elements in no given view
notInView.description: With `skipNotInView`: the elements left out of a test case because they apply in none of the given views, counted once per test case and element; a test case with no element left is marked (see `skipNotInView`). Information only: it does not change the exit code.

unknown.title: Unknown references
unknown.description: Each reference that names no element or more than one, with its test case; that test case stays unchanged. Each gives an error problem, so the call fails (CLI exit code 1).

line.title: Line
line.description: The line of the `<testcase>` in the file as read.

ref.title: Reference
ref.description: The reference as the test case gives it.

files.title: Files
files.description: The written file, relative to the workspace root (the folder of the main repository) with `/` when it lies below it or in another repository of the workspace, else its absolute path. None when nothing is written: nothing to change in place, or `output` holds these bytes already; a given `output` is otherwise written even when nothing changes.

commands.title: Show verification status
commands.summary: Verification status of a selection per view, from the evidence records and, without own record, from the children; validation status from the validation records.
commands.details: The verification status comes from the evidence records and, without own record, from the children, with the children that are missing; the validation status from the validation records. Without a selection every element of the workspace is listed, and only requirements, needs and elements with a validation record carry a status, so select them, for example by type.

selection.description: The elements whose verification status is given; without it every element.

limit.description: The most elements on one page.

elements.title: Elements
elements.description: One page of the selection in workspace order, each element as element.list gives it, with `verification` for every element whose type has the meaning `requirement`: its verification status in each view it is in by the view rule: the core when it has no validity, each variant it is in; none for a variant that excludes or replaces it or whose status the metamodel marks invalid, and for a requirement without own verification record in a view its indirect verification from its children (`indirect`) or the children that are missing (`missingChildren`); an element marked emergent is never `indirect`; and `validation`, the validation status (`$defs/element` `validation`: every need, a requirement with a validation record). Derived from the evidence records; it is not the element's `status` and never changes it. While the metamodel is not valid the records are not compared: every requirement is `open`, every need `open`, and no other element has `validation`.

total.title: Total
total.description: Every element of the selection, not only the page.

commands.details: The folder is new, empty, or holds an earlier HTML export (its marker file `reqseq-html-export.yaml`): then the files that export wrote are replaced or removed, and every other file stays as it is and is named as a problem. Texts are written as text where they would run, load or link something outside the folder (raw HTML, links with another scheme than http, https or mailto, images from the network or outside the element's repository, Mermaid diagrams with click actions or HTML labels), each named as a problem. Formulas are set when the pages are written, and Mermaid diagrams are drawn by one copy of the library in the folder; a formula with an error shows its source and the error and is named as a problem. On an error the earlier export stays as it was.
